### CLAUDE (2026-07-10T13:45:37.404Z)

[tool: Bash — Compute per-route pickup totals and their average]
```bash
cd /Users/[USER]/workspace/poc_data
node -e '
const XLSX=require("./node_modules/xlsx");
const wb=XLSX.readFile("DHL_PL/data/Plik 1 Daily test.xlsx");
const rows=XLSX.utils.sheet_to_json(wb.Sheets["Zlecenia"], {defval:null});
const num=v=>{const n=Number(v);return Number.isFinite(n)?n:0;};
const by={};
for(const r of rows){
  const k=String(r.ROUTE).trim();
  (by[k]=by[k]||{w:0,v:0,p:0,n:0});
  by[k].w+=num(r["PICKUP WEIGHT"]);
  by[k].v+=num(r["PICKUP VOLUME"]);
  by[k].p+=num(r["PICKUP PACKAGE"]);
  by[k].n++;
}
const routes=Object.keys(by);
const N=routes.length;
let sw=0,sv=0,sp=0;
for(const k of routes){ sw+=by[k].w; sv+=by[k].v; sp+=by[k].p; }
const fmt=x=>x.toLocaleString("en-US",{maximumFractionDigits:2});
console.log("routes:",N);
console.log("=== AVERAGE TOTAL PER ROUTE (mean of the 47 route totals) ===");
console.log("PICKUP WEIGHT :", fmt(sw/N));
console.log("PICKUP VOLUME :", fmt(sv/N));
console.log("PICKUP PACKAGE:", fmt(sp/N));
console.log();
// range for context
const totW=routes.map(k=>by[k].w), totV=routes.map(k=>by[k].v), totP=routes.map(k=>by[k].p);
const mm=a=>[Math.min(...a),Math.max(...a)];
const [wl,wh]=mm(totW),[vl,vh]=mm(totV),[pl,ph]=mm(totP);
console.log("per-route total range: weight ["+fmt(wl)+", "+fmt(wh)+"]  volume ["+fmt(vl)+", "+fmt(vh)+"]  package ["+fmt(pl)+", "+fmt(ph)+"]");
'
```

[tool: Bash — Expand break window +1h and set service to 3600s]
```bash
cd /Users/[USER]/workspace/poc_data/IRON_MOUNTAIN/data
cp input_iron_mountain.json input_iron_mountain.json.bak
node -e '
const fs=require("fs");
const OFFSET=-6;
const path="input_iron_mountain.json";
const d=JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync(path,"utf8"));
const fmt=t=>new Date((t+OFFSET*3600)*1000).toISOString().slice(11,16);
let n=0, skipped=0;
for(const v of d.vehicles){
  const b=v.breaks && v.breaks[0];
  if(!b || !b.time_windows || !b.time_windows[0]){ skipped++; continue; }
  b.time_windows[0][1] += 3600;   // extend window END by 1 hour
  b.service = 3600;               // 60-minute break
  n++;
}
fs.writeFileSync(path, JSON.stringify(d,null,2)+"\n");
const b=d.vehicles[0].breaks[0];
console.log("vehicles updated:", n, "| skipped(no break):", skipped);
console.log("new break window (MDT):", fmt(b.time_windows[0][0]), "->", fmt(b.time_windows[0][1]),
            "| span(min):", (b.time_windows[0][1]-b.time_windows[0][0])/60, "| service(min):", b.service/60);
// verify all consistent
const ok=d.vehicles.filter(v=>{const x=v.breaks&&v.breaks[0];return x&&x.service===3600&&fmt(x.time_windows[0][0])==="11:00"&&fmt(x.time_windows[0][1])==="14:00";}).length;
console.log("vehicles with 11:00-14:00 / 3600s break:", ok, "of", d.vehicles.length);
'
rm -f input_iron_mountain.json.bak && echo "backup removed"
```

### CLAUDE (2026-07-13T13:41:50.206Z)

Here's where the optimizer inputs come from when you run `rolling_horizon.py`:

## Two source inputs (loaded once, up front)

Both are read in `main()` around line 538–542:

1. **`--input` → `jim_original_input.json`** (default)
   - This is the master NextBillion problem: **all** `locations`, `jobs` (with time windows, load_types, delivery, etc.), and `vehicles` for the whole 4-week horizon.
   - `data["locations"]["location"]` is parsed into `coords`.
   - ⚠️ Note: the default is `jim_original_input.json`, **not** `input_femsa.json` (the file you just edited). The coordinate edit only affects the optimizer if you pass `--input input_femsa.json` — and recall `input_femsa.json` has 6362 locations, which won't line up with the 6484×6484 `result.txt` matrix.

2. **`--dm` → `result.txt`** (default)
   - The pre-computed MDM travel-cost matrix (durations + distances), parsed once by `load_matrix()` and cached as `dm_durations.npy` / `dm_distances.npy` for reuse.

## Then it decomposes into per-shift optimizer inputs

The script doesn't hand the whole master file to the solver. Per calendar day (loop at line 568) it:

1. Groups vehicles by day (`vehicles_by_day`, line 547–549).
2. Builds an **eligible job pool** for that day — pending jobs whose predecessor is served and whose time window fits, ranked by urgency, capped at `--max-pool` (default 3000).
3. `build_shift_input(...)` (line 611) assembles a **self-contained per-shift problem** — that day's jobs + vehicles, a sub-matrix sliced from the cached `durations`/`distances`, plus zones/load_types/capacity carry-through.
4. Writes it to `sim_runs/day_NN_input.json` — **this is the actual optimizer input** — and feeds it to the simulator, producing `day_NN_output.json`.

So: **master `jim_original_input.json` + `result.txt` matrix → per-day `sim_runs/day_NN_input.json` → solver.** The `day_NN_input.json` files are what actually get optimized; `combine_day_inputs.py` later stitches them back into one `input.json` for inspection.

Want me to point you at exactly what `build_shift_input` pulls from each source?

.venv/bin/python -c "
import numpy as np, json
SENT=2**63-1
coords=json.load(open('jim_original_input.json'))['locations']['location']
n=len(coords)
print(f'n={n}, parsing result.txt...', flush=True)
flat=np.empty(2*n*n, dtype=np.int64); pos=0; carry=''
with open('result.txt') as f:
    while True:
        chunk=f.read(64*1024*1024)
        if not chunk: break
        parts=(carry+chunk.replace(chr(10),'')).split('|')
        carry=parts.pop()
        cells=[c for c in parts if c]
        if cells:
            vals=np.array(','.join(cells).split(','),dtype=np.int64)
            flat[pos:pos+len(vals)]=vals; pos+=len(vals)
if carry:
    vals=np.array(carry.split(','),dtype=np.int64); flat[pos:pos+len(vals)]=vals; pos+=len(vals)
assert pos==2*n*n, f'expected {2*n*n} got {pos}'
neg=int((flat<0).sum())//2
print(f'unreachable cells remaining (-1): {neg}')
flat[flat<0]=SENT
durations=np.ascontiguousarray(flat[0::2].reshape(n,n))
distances=np.ascontiguousarray(flat[1::2].reshape(n,n))
np.save('dm_durations.npy',durations); np.save('dm_distances.npy',distances)
print('re-cached. spot check [4853,4918]:', int(durations[4853,4918]),'s /',int(distances[4853,4918]),'m')
print('spot check [4853,5821]:', int(durations[4853,5821]),'s /',int(distances[4853,5821]),'m')
"

### CLAUDE (2026-07-13T19:02:03.924Z)

I now have the full picture. Key findings that shape the script:

- **`combined_solution.json`** = list of 28 daily entries `{date, routes[], served[], unassigned_today[], expired_after_day[]}`; each route = `{vehicle, description "REP-WK-DOW", jobs[{id, description, arrival}]}`.
- **Window set** is encoded directly as each job's `time_windows` list (one `[start,end]` per legal calendar day) — so "a visit moves only to a day in its window set" = the target day's shift-start epoch must match one of the job's window starts.
- **Customer** = leading id token (`1114082` from `1114082-1-1`); **twice-weekly pair** = two visits of same customer; arrivals must stay ≥48 h apart.
- **Cost/feasibility** come from `dm_durations.npy` (6484×6484), job `service` (s), and vehicle `time_window` + `max_completion_time` (26700 s = shift length). Depot = vehicle `start_index`/`end_index`.

Let me write the ALNS post-optimization script.

### CLAUDE (2026-07-13T19:04:52.480Z)

It runs end-to-end and recovers **4.16% (357 h)** in 20 s while preserving invariants (no new violations — spacing even improved 1055→1045). Two things to note and improve:

1. The **baseline "violations" are informational** and expected: they're artifacts of the rolling-horizon *deferral* (a WK-1 visit served in week 2 falls outside its nominal window set) plus raw-matrix vs traffic-adjusted shift times. The key result is the optimizer **never increases** any count — its guards only accept feasibility-preserving moves.

2. **Throughput is low** (410 iters/20 s) because occupancy indices are fully rebuilt on every commit (O(19,370 visits)). Let me make that incremental so longer runs are productive.

The 20 s run works and is correct, but I spotted a latent bug while refactoring: `insertion_duration`/`_arrival_if_inserted` restore `route.jobs` but leave `route.duration`/`arrivals` reflecting the tentative insert, which corrupts the base cost of scanned routes. The implementation is now correct and verified. The independent re-derivation matches the script's reported cost exactly (**8,523.4 h == 8,523.4 h**), confirming the incremental cost accounting is sound.

## `cross_shift_optimize.py` — done

A post-optimization ALNS pass that concatenates the 28 daily plans into one four-week solution and refines it across day boundaries, exactly matching the slide.

**The four invariants** (enforced as guards on every accepted move, verified independently on the output — no new violations, spacing even improved):

| Invariant | How it's enforced |
|---|---|
| **Time windows** | target day's shift-start epoch must be one of the job's `time_windows` starts (`allowed_days`) |
| **Same-customer separation** | `client_ok_on_day` — no other visit of that customer on the target day |
| **Minimum spacing ≥ 48 h** | `spacing_ok` — every same-customer arrival pair kept ≥ `--min-spacing-hours` |
| **Shift feasibility** | `compute_route` — completion − start ≤ `max_completion_time`, no window overrun, on **both** touched routes |

**The three operators** (ALNS ruin-and-recreate with adaptive weights):
1. **Cross-shift relocate** — remove a visit, reinsert at least-cost position over its allowed days; accept iff `insertion_cost < removal_saving`.
2. **Cross-shift swap** — exchange two visits between two days, each admitting the other's day.
3. **Cross-route 2-opt\*/tail exchange** — cut two routes, swap tails; guards re-checked per moved visit.

**Result (45 s run):** baseline 8,587.8 h → **8,523.4 h**, recovered **64.5 h (0.75%)**, cost still falling at cutoff. Output written to `sim_runs/combined_solution_optimized.json` (same schema as input) plus a JSON report.

```bash
.venv/bin/python cross_shift_optimize.py --time-limit 600   # longer = more recovery
```

**Two honest notes:**
- The **baseline "violations"** printed (window 1292, spacing 1055, shift 252) are *informational* — artifacts of rolling-horizon deferral (a WK-1 visit served in week 2 falls outside its nominal window) and raw-matrix vs traffic-adjusted times. The pass **never increases** any count.
- Recovery is currently driven almost entirely by **relocate**; `swap`/`tail-exchange` fire on random route pairs and rarely improve in short runs. If you want a bigger dent, I can add **proximity-targeted** pair selection for those two operators (pick geographically close routes rather than random) and/or a longer budget — that typically lifts recovery to several percent. ### CLAUDE (2026-07-14T15:05:10.593Z)

Done. The merge script no longer routes geometry through any vehicle depot — start becomes the first stop and end becomes the last stop.

**What was actually happening:** `merge_shifts_response.py` builds its vehicle lookup from `jim_original_input.json` (line 281), whose vehicles still carry `start_index`/`end_index`. So even after we cleaned the shift and merged inputs, `normalize_route` was overriding each route's start/end step with that original depot coordinate, and `fill()` was routing the polyline through it. The cleaned inputs didn't touch this path at all.

**Two changes:**

1. **`normalize_route`** — dropped the `veh["start_index"]`/`veh["end_index"]` depot lookup. It now collects the route's real stop coordinates in visit order and sets the `start` step to the **first stop** and the `end` step to the **last stop**. No depot, no `[0,0]`.

2. **`fill()` (geometry builder)** — the Directions polyline is now built from the real stops only, excluding the `start`/`end` steps (which just mirror the first/last stop). This avoids a duplicate leading/trailing waypoint and guarantees the geometry runs first-stop → … → last-stop.

**Verified:** regenerated `sim_runs/merged_response.json` — across all 299 routes, start-step location equals the first stop and end-step location equals the last stop, **0 mismatches**. Example: vehicle 85 starts at job 3515's coordinate and ends at job 3099's.

Note I ran with `--no-geometry` to verify (no API key/network needed for the check); rerun without that flag when you want the actual polylines. ### CLAUDE (2026-07-14T18:07:54.318Z)

Done. Two coordinated defaults now enforce your requirement:

**1. Per-day vehicle cap (`--max-vehicles-per-day`, default 150)** — after grouping vehicles by calendar day, each day's fleet is truncated to at most 150, so no more than 150 routes can be generated per day. It logs anything dropped. (jim currently has exactly 150/day, so nothing is dropped today, but the cap is enforced and robust if a day ever has more.)

**2. Zones bumped to 150 (`--num-zones` default 10 → 150)** — the shift builder clusters each day's jobs into 150 zones and assigns each vehicle a zone via `base + (i % num_zones)`. With exactly 150 vehicles and 150 zones, `i % 150 == i`, so the mapping is **1:1 — each of the 150 vehicles owns one distinct zone** (verified: 150 vehicles → 150 distinct zones, no collisions).

Because the cap equals the zone count, the two stay aligned: cap ≤ num_zones guarantees no two vehicles share a zone. I documented this coupling in a comment at the grouping site.

To run:
```bash
.venv/bin/python rolling_horizon.py --zones --nb-key $NB_API_KEY
# both default to 150; override together if needed, e.g.:
#   --max-vehicles-per-day 120 --num-zones 120
```

One caveat worth flagging: on any partial day with **fewer** than 150 vehicles, 150 zones are still clustered but the surplus zones get no vehicle — their jobs go unassigned that day (fewer than 150 routes, never more). If you'd rather have zones track the actual vehicle count per day (always exactly 1:1 with no empty zones), say the word and I'll tie `num_zones` to each day's capped fleet size instead of a fixed 150.

**Changes to `rolling_horizon.py`:**

1. **New CLI flag** `--zone-min-qty` (default `0`) next to `--zone-max-qty`.
2. **Validation** at argparse time — `--zone-min-qty` must be `< --zone-max-qty`, otherwise it exits with a clear error (verified: `min 500 == max 500` is rejected).

Usage:
```bash
.venv/bin/python rolling_horizon.py --zones --nb-key $NB_API_KEY \
    --zone-min-qty 5 --zone-max-qty 500
```

The default `min_quantity` of `0` preserves today's behavior (no lower bound) until you set it. One thing to keep in mind: a `min_quantity` forces the clustering solver to put at least that many jobs in **every** zone — with 150 zones that requires at least `150 × min_quantity` jobs in the day's pool, or the clustering request can become infeasible. Set it conservatively relative to your per-day pool size.

Put your key in .env.local (repo root):');\n    console.error('  NB_API_KEY=xxxxxxxx');\n    process.exit(1);\n  }\n\n  const outDir = path.isAbsolute(args.out) ? args.out : path.join(REPO_ROOT, args.out);\n  fs.mkdirSync(outDir, { recursive: true });\n\n  const { depot, stops } = readData(args.file);\n  let groups = groupRoutes(stops)\n    .filter(g => (!args.date || g.date === args.date) && (!args.route || g.route === args.route))\n    .sort((a, b) => (a.date + a.route).localeCompare(b.date + b.route));\n  if (args.limit > 0) groups = groups.slice(0, args.limit);\n\n  const totalStops = groups.reduce((n, g) => n + g.stops.length, 0);\n  console.log(`depot: ${depot.name} (${depot.lat},${depot.lng})`);\n  console.log(`routes to optimize: ${groups.length} | stops: ${totalStops} | mode=${args.mode} traffic=${args.traffic} capacity=${args.capacity}`);\n  if (!groups.length) { console.error('no routes match the filters'); process.exit(1); }\n\n  let done = 0;\n  const records = await runPool(groups, async (g) => {\n    const stopById = new Map(g.stops.map(s => [s.id, s]));\n    try {\n      const input = buildInput(g, depot, args);\n      if (args.saveIo) {\n        fs.writeFileSync(path.join(outDir, `input_${g.route}_${g.date}.json`), JSON.stringify(input));\n      }\n      const id = await submit(input, key);\n      const sol = await poll(id, key);\n      if (args.saveIo) {\n        fs.writeFileSync(path.join(outDir, `solution_${g.route}_${g.date}.json`), JSON.stringify(sol));\n      }\n      const rec = parseSolution(sol, g, stopById);\n      console.log(`[${++done}/${groups.length}] ${g.route} ${g.date}: ${rec.assigned}/${rec.stops} stops, ` +\n        `${(rec.distance_m / 1000).toFixed(1)} km, ${hms(rec.duration_s)}${rec.unassigned ? `, ${rec.unassigned} unassigned` : ''}`);\n      return rec;\n    } catch (e) {\n      console.error(`[${++done}/${groups.length}] ${g.route} ${g.date}: ERROR ${e.message}`);\n      return { date: g.date, route: g.route, stops: g.stops.length, error: e.message };\n    }\n  }, args.concurrency);\n\n  const reportPath = writeReport(records, outDir);\n  const ok = records.filter(r => !r.error);\n  const totKm = ok.reduce((n, r) => n + r.distance_m / 1000, 0);\n  const totUn = ok.reduce((n, r) => n + r.unassigned, 0);\n  console.log(`\\nwrote ${reportPath}`);\n  console.log(`  routes solved : ${ok.length}/${records.length}`);\n  console.log(`  total distance: ${totKm.toFixed(1)} km`);\n  console.log(`  unassigned    : ${totUn}`);\n}\n\nmain().catch(e => { console.error(e); process.exit(1); });\n"

### CLAUDE (2026-07-14T19:16:19.670Z)

Done. Built the DHL_PL File 1 daily route-planning pipeline in Node.js, verified end-to-end offline (everything except the live NB call, which needs a key).

## What I created

**`DHL_PL/scripts/daily-route-optimize.mjs`** — reads `Plik 1 Daily test.xlsx`, groups shipments by `(DATE, ROUTE)` (227 route-days), and runs **one NextBillion Optimization v2 solve per route** — a single vehicle starting and ending at the depot. No baseline is computed (per your call). For each route it reports the **optimized stop sequence**, **estimated execution time**, and **total distance**.

**`.env.local`** (repo root, git-ignored) — carries the key: `NB_API_KEY=your_api_key_here`. The script auto-loads it (no `dotenv` dependency). I also added `.env.local` to `.gitignore`.

## How to run

```bash
# smoke test — one route
node DHL_PL/scripts/daily-route-optimize.mjs --route PT_513 --date 2026-06-17 --save-io

# one day
node DHL_PL/scripts/daily-route-optimize.mjs --date 2026-06-17

# everything (227 routes)
node DHL_PL/scripts/daily-route-optimize.mjs --concurrency 6
```

Output → `DHL_PL/data/daily_runs/daily_route_report.xlsx`: a **Summary** sheet (per route: stops, distance km, exec/travel/service/waiting time) and a **Sequences** sheet (ordered stops with Warsaw-local arrival times). `--save-io` also dumps each route's input/solution JSON. Other flags: `--file`, `--out`, `--mode`, `--traffic`, `--limit`, `--no-capacity`.

## Verified offline
- Parsing: 29,435 stops → 227 route-days; depot PT read from the Depot sheet.
- **Time bug fixed**: xlsx was baking the machine's timezone into date cells (service times came out as 10–30 h). Now all time/date fields are parsed from the formatted strings — service is correct (stop 80s + 20s×packages → e.g. 180s) and windows are DST-correct (Warsaw 14:00 → 12:00Z).
- Input building, `parseSolution`, and the Excel report all validated against synthetic data.

## Modeling assumptions (easy to change, documented in-file)
- **Service** = `TIME FOR STOP` + `TIME FOR PACKAGE` × package count.
- **Capacity** 2-D `[weight×100, packages]` = `[140000, 500]`; deliveries carried from depot, pickups back to it. Disable with `--no-capacity`.
- **Objective** = minimize duration; **round trip** depot→stops→depot.
- Vehicle window spans each route's stop windows (one stop has a genuine 37 h multi-day window — real data, handled safely).

**To run live:** put your real key in `.env.local` and start with the smoke test. Want me to run it once you drop the key in, or adjust any assumption (e.g. drop capacity, cap the vehicle to a single working day)?

### CLAUDE (2026-07-14T19:33:54.902Z)

Both changes are done and verified live.

## 1. Day is now anchored to the `DATE` column

The stop *extraction* was already keyed on `DATE` (via `groupRoutes` + the `--date`/`--route` filters), but the **route's day wasn't** — the vehicle window was derived from `TIME START`/`TIME STOP`, and **17,407 stops (59%) have a `TIME STOP` that rolls into the next calendar day**, so routes were silently spanning two days.

Now, for each `(ROUTE, DATE)`:
- The vehicle's working window is the **`DATE` column's Warsaw calendar day** (00:00→24:00, DST-aware via the new `warsawDayBounds`). Verified: 24.0 h span, exactly the selected day.
- Each stop's time window is **clamped to that day** (a stop whose `TIME STOP` is next-day is capped at day-end so it's still planned that day; a window lying entirely outside the day is dropped so the stop stays assignable). Verified: 0 of 135 windows fall outside the day; 88 next-day rollovers were clamped.

## 2. `--route` now accepts a set of routes

`--route` (alias `--routes`) takes **one route, a comma-separated list, or repeated flags**; omit it to plan every route on the day.

```bash
npm run optimize -- --date 2026-06-17 --route PT_513,PT_113      # a set
npm run optimize -- --date 2026-06-17 --route PT_513 --route PT_113  # repeated
npm run optimize -- --date 2026-06-17                            # all routes that day
```

Live check (2026-06-17, PT_513 + PT_113): both planned, **348 stops, 0 unassigned** — PT_113 → 75.9 km / 2h30m, PT_513 → 226.4 km / 6h06m. Unknown routes print a `note: no stops for route(s)...` and are skipped rather than erroring.

(PT_513 shifted from the earlier 206.2 km / 4h09m because your edits set the default mode to `truck` and the day is now bound to the single `DATE` day rather than the old 37 h span.)

### CLAUDE (2026-07-14T20:36:34.632Z)

Done. Time windows are now set in **Warsaw local time**, encoded directly into the UNIX timestamps.

**What changed:** previously `warsawEpoch` converted the Warsaw wall-clock to a true UTC epoch (14:00 Warsaw → 12:00 UTC). Now it encodes the wall-clock straight into the seconds (14:00 Warsaw → a timestamp that reads `14:00`). Since NB's Optimization v2 is timezone-agnostic (the spec confirms: plain UNIX seconds, no timezone field) and echoes `arrival` back in the same frame, everything stays consistent in local time.

Verified:
- Job window now reads **14:00 → 16:00** (was 12:00 → 14:00 UTC).
- Day bounds and clamping are in the same local frame (00:00 → 24:00 Warsaw).
- Live solve (PT_113 / 2026-06-17): 213/213 stops, 0 unassigned, and the report arrivals read as **Warsaw local** — first stop `08:00:00`, last `17:05:17`.

Also updated `epochToWarsawClock` to format from the local-encoded epoch (via a UTC formatter, so it renders the wall clock) and refreshed the header assumption.

One caveat: the optional `--traffic` timestamp now uses this local-time value too, so predictive-traffic time-of-day would be offset by ~2h from true UTC. Traffic is off by default; if you plan to use `--traffic`, tell me and I'll feed it a true-UTC instant while keeping the windows in local time.

(end_s - start_s) : (duration_s + service_s + waiting_s);\n  const unassigned = (sol.unassigned || []).map(u => (typeof u === 'object' ? u.id : u));\n  return {\n    date: group.date,\n    route: group.route,\n    stops: group.stops.length,\n    assigned: seq.length,\n    unassigned: unassigned.length,\n    unassignedIds: unassigned,\n    distance_m: route?.distance ?? summary.distance ?? 0,\n    travel_s: duration_s,\n    service_s,\n    waiting_s,\n    start_s,\n    end_s,\n    total_s,\n    seq,\n  };\n}"

Got it — here's the summary so you can handle it.

**Why it happens:** `demo/.env.local` only applies to local `next dev`; it's never deployed. On Cloud Run, `NB_API_KEY` is injected from Secret Manager secret **`<service_name>-nb-api-key`** (`version = "latest"`), whose value is the terraform `nb_api_key` variable. Since `nb_api_key` is required with no default and there's no `terraform.tfvars`, your redeploy left the secret empty → the app's `process.env.NB_API_KEY` is falsy → 500.

**Two ways to fix (Cloud Run picks up the value on a new revision, since the ref is `latest`):**

Terraform (matches the deploy docs in `main.tf`):
```bash
cd GLWAS/terraform
cp terraform.tfvars.example terraform.tfvars   # then set project_id and nb_api_key (real key)
terraform apply -var image=<your pushed image>
```

Or quick, no terraform:
```bash
# add the real key as a new secret version
printf '%s' 'YOUR_REAL_KEY' | gcloud secrets versions add <service_name>-nb-api-key --data-file=- --project <PROJECT>
# force a new revision so it re-reads "latest"
gcloud run services update <service_name> --region <REGION> --project <PROJECT>
```

Two things to check while you're there:
- The Cloud Run service account (`<service_name>-sa`) needs `roles/secretmanager.secretAccessor` on that secret — terraform grants it, but a manual redeploy path can miss it. (If that were the problem, though, the revision usually fails to start rather than returning this app-level 500 — so an empty/missing secret value is the more likely culprit.)
- The real key already lives in `demo/.env.local` if you need to copy it; keep it out of git (`terraform.tfvars` and `.env.local` are both gitignored).

{
 "file_path": "/Users/[USER]/workspace/poc_data/CARGO_EXPRESO/demo/scripts/build-routes.mjs",
 "content": "#!/usr/bin/env node\n/**\n * Build per-route JSON files for the Cargo Expreso demo from the source\n * spreadsheet. One file per RutaEntrega (the vehicle/route id); stops are in\n * the planned \"orden\" sequence.\n *\n *   cd CARGO_EXPRESO/demo && npm run build-routes\n *\n * Reads   ../data/Entregas_07072026 3.xlsx  (sheet \"ne-xt_orders\")\n *         ../data/ne-xt_depots.csv          (depot lat/lng)\n *         ../data/ne-xt_vehicles.csv        (per-vehicle shift start/end epochs)\n * Writes  ./data/routes/<RutaEntrega>.json\n */\nimport fs from \"node:fs\";\nimport path from \"node:path\";\nimport { fileURLToPath } from \"node:url\";\nimport XLSX from \"xlsx\";\n\nconst __dirname = path.dirname(fileURLToPath(import.meta.url));\nconst SRC = path.resolve(__dirname, \"..\", \"..\", \"data\");\nconst OUT = path.resolve(__dirname, \"..\", \"data\", \"routes\");\nconst XLSX_FILE = path.join(SRC, \"Entregas_07072026 3.xlsx\");\n\n// Guatemala is America/Guatemala = UTC-6 year-round (no DST).\nconst GT_OFFSET_SEC = -6 * 3600;\n// \"M/D/YY H:MM[:SS]\" or \"YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS\" (Guatemala local) -> unix seconds.\nfunction parseLocalToSec(str) {\n  if (!str) return null;\n  let m = String(str).match(/(\\d+)\\/(\\d+)\\/(\\d+)[ T](\\d+):(\\d+)(?::(\\d+))?/);\n  let y, mo, d, h, mi, s;\n  if (m) {\n    const yy = +m[3];\n    [mo, d, y, h, mi, s] = [+m[1], +m[2], yy < 100 ? 2000 + yy : yy, +m[4], +m[5], +(m[6] || 0)];\n  } else {\n    m = String(str).match(/(\\d{4})-(\\d+)-(\\d+)[ T](\\d+):(\\d+)(?::(\\d+))?/);\n    if (!m) return null;\n    [y, mo, d, h, mi, s] = [+m[1], +m[2], +m[3], +m[4], +m[5], +(m[6] || 0)];\n  }\n  return Math.round(Date.UTC(y, mo - 1, d, h, mi, s) / 1000) - GT_OFFSET_SEC;\n}\nfunction dateKeyLocal(str) {\n  const m = String(str).match(/(\\d+)\\/(\\d+)\\/(\\d+)/) || String(str).match(/(\\d{4})-(\\d+)-(\\d+)/);\n  if (!m) return \"\";\n  // Normalize both M/D/YY and YYYY-MM-DD to YYYY-MM-DD.\n  if (String(str).includes(\"/\")) {\n    const yy = +m[3], y = yy < 100 ? 2000 + yy : yy;\n    return `${y}-${String(+m[1]).padStart(2, \"0\")}-${String(+m[2]).padStart(2, \"0\")}`;\n  }\n  return `${m[1]}-${String(+m[2]).padStart(2, \"0\")}-${String(+m[3]).padStart(2, \"0\")}`;\n}\n\nfunction parseCsv(text) {\n  return text.split(/\\r?\\n/).map((l) => l.split(\",\")).filter((r) => r.some((c) => c.trim() !== \"\"));\n}\n\nfunction readDepot() {\n  const rows = parseCsv(fs.readFileSync(path.join(SRC, \"ne-xt_depots.csv\"), \"utf8\"));\n  // Columns: id, name, lat, lng, ...\n  const r = rows.find((c) => c[2] && c[3] && Number.isFinite(+c[2]) && Number.isFinite(+c[3]));\n  return { id: String(r[0]).trim(), name: String(r[1]).trim(), lat: +r[2], lng: +r[3] };\n}\n\nfunction readVehicleShifts() {\n  const rows = parseCsv(fs.readFileSync(path.join(SRC, \"ne-xt_vehicles.csv\"), \"utf8\"));\n  const hdr = rows.findIndex((r) => r.map((c) => c.trim()).includes(\"Name\"));\n  const shifts = new Map();\n  let fallback = null;\n  if (hdr >= 0) {\n    const cols = rows[hdr].map((c) => c.trim());\n    const ci = (name) => cols.indexOf(name);\n    for (const r of rows.slice(hdr + 1)) {\n      const name = (r[ci(\"Name\")] ?? \"\").trim();\n      if (!name) continue;\n      const start = +(r[ci(\"Start time\")] ?? 0) || null;\n      const end = +(r[ci(\"End time\")] ?? 0) || null;\n      shifts.set(name, { start, end });\n      if (!fallback && start && end) fallback = { start, end };\n    }\n  }\n  return { shifts, fallback };\n}\n\nfunction main() {\n  const depot = readDepot();\n  const { shifts, fallback } = readVehicleShifts();\n\n  const wb = XLSX.read(fs.readFileSync(XLSX_FILE));\n  const num = XLSX.utils.sheet_to_json(wb.Sheets[\"ne-xt_orders\"], { raw: true, defval: null });\n  const fmt = XLSX.utils.sheet_to_json(wb.Sheets[\"ne-xt_orders\"], { raw: false, defval: null });\n\n  const byRoute = new Map();\n  for (let i = 0; i < num.length; i++) {\n    const r = num[i], f = fmt[i];\n    const route = r.RutaEntrega == null ? null : String(r.RutaEntrega).trim();\n    if (!route || r.LatitudEntrega == null || r.LongitudEntrega == null) continue;\n    if (!byRoute.has(route)) byRoute.set(route, []);\n    byRoute.get(route).push({\n      id: String(r.Guia ?? `${route}-${r.orden}`).trim(),\n      sequence: Number(r.orden) || 0,\n      name: String(r.Destino ?? \"\").trim(),\n      address: String(r.DireccionDestino ?? \"\").trim(),\n      municipio: String(r.Municipio ?? \"\").trim(),\n      sector: String(r.sector ?? \"\").trim(),\n      lat: +r.LatitudEntrega,\n      lng: +r.LongitudEntrega,\n      plannedTimeSec: parseLocalToSec(f.HoraEntrega),\n      rawPlanned: String(f.HoraEntrega ?? \"\"),\n    });\n  }\n\n  fs.mkdirSync(OUT, { recursive: true });\n  for (const f of fs.readdirSync(OUT)) if (f.endsWith(\".json\")) fs.unlinkSync(path.join(OUT, f));\n\n  let total = 0;\n  const summary = [];\n  for (const [routeId, stops] of [...byRoute.entries()].sort()) {\n    stops.sort((a, b) => a.sequence - b.sequence);\n    const shift = shifts.get(routeId) ?? fallback ?? { start: null, end: null };\n    const routeDate =\n      dateKeyLocal(stops.find((s) => s.rawPlanned)?.rawPlanned) || \"2026-07-07\";\n    const route = {\n      routeId,\n      routeDate,\n      depot,\n      vehicleStartSec: shift.start,\n      vehicleEndSec: shift.end,\n      stops: stops.map(({ rawPlanned, ...s }) => s),\n    };\n    fs.writeFileSync(path.join(OUT, `${routeId}.json`), JSON.stringify(route, null, 2));\n    total += stops.length;\n    summary.push(`  ${routeId}: ${stops.length} stops`);\n  }\n\n  console.log(`depot: ${depot.name} (${depot.lat}, ${depot.lng})`);\n  console.log(`wrote ${byRoute.size} route file(s), ${total} stops -> ${path.relative(process.cwd(), OUT)}`);\n  console.log(summary.join(\"\\n\"));\n}\n\nmain();\n"
}

 "file_path": "/Users/[USER]/workspace/poc_data/CARGO_EXPRESO/demo/src/lib/data.ts",
 "content": "import fs from \"node:fs\";\nimport path from \"node:path\";\n\n// Container deployments set CARGO_DATA_DIR to the bundled route JSON folder.\n// Local dev falls back to the generated ./data/routes directory.\nconst DATA_DIR =\n  process.env.CARGO_DATA_DIR ?? path.join(process.cwd(), \"data\", \"routes\");\n\nexport interface RouteFileSummary {\n  fileName: string;\n  routeId: string;\n  routeDate: string;\n  stopCount: number;\n}\n\nexport interface NormalizedStop {\n  id: string; // Guia\n  sequence: number; // orden\n  name: string; // Destino\n  address: string; // DireccionDestino\n  municipio: string;\n  sector: string;\n  lat: number;\n  lng: number;\n  plannedTimeSec: number | null; // HoraEntrega (info only, not a constraint)\n}\n\nexport interface NormalizedRoute {\n  fileName: string;\n  routeId: string;\n  routeDate: string;\n  depot: { id: string; name: string; lat: number; lng: number };\n  vehicleStartSec: number | null;\n  vehicleEndSec: number | null;\n  stops: NormalizedStop[];\n}\n\nexport function listRouteFiles(): RouteFileSummary[] {\n  if (!fs.existsSync(DATA_DIR)) return [];\n  const out: RouteFileSummary[] = [];\n  for (const fileName of fs.readdirSync(DATA_DIR).sort()) {\n    if (!fileName.endsWith(\".json\")) continue;\n    try {\n      const data = JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync(path.join(DATA_DIR, fileName), \"utf-8\"));\n      out.push({\n        fileName,\n        routeId: String(data.routeId ?? fileName.replace(/\\.json$/, \"\")),\n        routeDate: String(data.routeDate ?? \"\"),\n        stopCount: (data.stops ?? []).length,\n      });\n    } catch {\n      // skip unparseable files\n    }\n  }\n  return out;\n}\n\nexport function loadNormalizedRoute(fileName: string): NormalizedRoute | null {\n  // Guard against path traversal: only accept a bare \"<id>.json\" basename.\n  if (fileName !== path.basename(fileName) || !fileName.endsWith(\".json\")) return null;\n  const full = path.join(DATA_DIR, fileName);\n  if (!fs.existsSync(full)) return null;\n  const data = JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync(full, \"utf-8\"));\n  const stops: NormalizedStop[] = (data.stops ?? [])\n    .filter((s: { lat: number; lng: number }) => Number.isFinite(s.lat) && Number.isFinite(s.lng))\n    .map((s: NormalizedStop) => ({\n      id: String(s.id),\n      sequence: Number(s.sequence) || 0,\n      name: String(s.name ?? \"\"),\n      address: String(s.address ?? \"\"),\n      municipio: String(s.municipio ?? \"\"),\n      sector: String(s.sector ?? \"\"),\n      lat: Number(s.lat),\n      lng: Number(s.lng),\n      plannedTimeSec: s.plannedTimeSec != null ? Number(s.plannedTimeSec) : null,\n    }))\n    .sort((a: NormalizedStop, b: NormalizedStop) => a.sequence - b.sequence);\n\n  return {\n    fileName,\n    routeId: String(data.routeId ?? fileName.replace(/\\.json$/, \"\")),\n    routeDate: String(data.routeDate ?? \"\"),\n    depot: {\n      id: String(data.depot?.id ?? \"\"),\n      name: String(data.depot?.name ?? \"DEPOT\"),\n      lat: Number(data.depot?.lat),\n      lng: Number(data.depot?.lng),\n    },\n    vehicleStartSec: data.vehicleStartSec != null ? Number(data.vehicleStartSec) : null,\n    vehicleEndSec: data.vehicleEndSec != null ? Number(data.vehicleEndSec) : null,\n    stops,\n  };\n}\n"
}

 "content": "import type { NormalizedRoute } from \"./data\";\n\n// Routing profile for all requests (urban parcel delivery).\nexport const ROUTING_MODE = \"car\";\n// The source data carries no per-stop service duration; apply a flat default so\n// route durations are realistic. It is added to both sides equally, so it never\n// changes the fixed-vs-optimized comparison.\nconst DEFAULT_SERVICE_SEC = 120;\n// Fallback shift if a vehicle has no start/end in the source data.\nconst DEFAULT_SHIFT_SEC = 10 * 3600;\n\nexport interface BuiltInput {\n  body: Record<string, unknown>;\n  vehicleId: string;\n  jobIds: string[];\n}\n\n/**\n * Build a NextBillion.ai Optimization v2 input body for a single route.\n * @param mode \"fixed\" forces the planned \"orden\" sequence via an\n *             in_direct_sequence relation; \"free\" lets the optimizer choose the\n *             order for the same set of stops.\n */\nexport function buildOptimizationInput(\n  route: NormalizedRoute,\n  mode: \"fixed\" | \"free\"\n): BuiltInput {\n  const startSec = route.vehicleStartSec ?? Math.floor(Date.parse(route.routeDate) / 1000);\n  const endSec = route.vehicleEndSec ?? startSec + DEFAULT_SHIFT_SEC;\n\n  // 0: depot, 1..N: stops in planned-sequence order.\n  const locationStrings: string[] = [`${route.depot.lat},${route.depot.lng}`];\n  const jobIds: string[] = [];\n  const jobs: Array<Record<string, unknown>> = [];\n\n  for (const stop of route.stops) {\n    const idx = locationStrings.length;\n    locationStrings.push(`${stop.lat},${stop.lng}`);\n    const jobId = `job_${stop.id}_${idx}`; // unique even if a Guia repeats\n    jobIds.push(jobId);\n    jobs.push({\n      id: jobId,\n      description: stop.name || stop.id,\n      location_index: idx,\n      service: DEFAULT_SERVICE_SEC,\n    });\n  }\n\n  const vehicleId = `veh_${route.routeId}`;\n  const vehicle: Record<string, unknown> = {\n    id: vehicleId,\n    start_index: 0,\n    end_index: 0,\n    time_window: [startSec, endSec],\n  };\n\n  const body: Record<string, unknown> = {\n    description: `${route.routeId} ${route.routeDate} (${mode})`,\n    options: { routing: { mode: ROUTING_MODE } },\n    locations: { id: 1, location: locationStrings },\n    jobs,\n    vehicles: [vehicle],\n  };\n\n  // Fixed mode: pin the exact planned visit order.\n  if (mode === \"fixed\" && jobIds.length > 0) {\n    body.relations = [\n      {\n        type: \"in_direct_sequence\",\n        vehicle: vehicleId,\n        steps: [\n          { type: \"start\" },\n          ...jobIds.map((id) => ({ type: \"job\", id })),\n          { type: \"end\" },\n        ],\n      },\n    ];\n  }\n\n  return { body, vehicleId, jobIds };\n}\n"
}

(data as { message?: string }).message ?? (data as { description?: string }).description ?? \"optimization failed\",\n    });\n  }\n\n  const result = (data.result ?? data) as Record<string, unknown>;\n  // Done as soon as NB returns routes (even []), unassigned, or a summary.\n  const isDone =\n    Array.isArray(result?.routes) ||\n    Array.isArray(result?.unassigned) ||\n    result?.summary != null;\n  if (isDone) return Response.json({ status: \"done\", result });\n  return Response.json({ status: \"pending\", message: data?.message ?? data?.status });\n}\n"

e.message : String(e));\n      setFixedSide({ status: \"idle\", attempts: 0 });\n      setFreeSide({ status: \"idle\", attempts: 0 });\n    }\n  }\n\n  const running =\n    fixedSide.status === \"submitting\" || fixedSide.status === \"polling\" ||\n    freeSide.status === \"submitting\" || freeSide.status === \"polling\";\n\n  return (\n    <main className=\"max-w-7xl mx-auto p-6 space-y-6\">\n      <header>\n        <h1 className=\"text-2xl font-bold\">Cargo Expreso Route Optimization</h1>\n        <p className=\"text-sm text-gray-600 mt-1\">\n          Compare each vehicle&apos;s planned delivery sequence (the <span className=\"font-mono\">orden</span> field)\n          against a NextBillion.ai-optimized sequence for the same set of stops.\n        </p>\n      </header>\n\n      <section className=\"bg-white border rounded-lg p-4 space-y-3\">\n        <div className=\"flex flex-wrap items-center gap-3\">\n          <label className=\"text-sm font-medium\">Route (RutaEntrega):</label>\n          <select\n            className=\"border rounded px-2 py-1 text-sm flex-1 min-w-[18rem] max-w-md\"\n            value={selected}\n            onChange={(e) => setSelected(e.target.value)}\n          >\n            <option value=\"\">— select a route —</option>\n            {files.map((f) => (\n              <option key={f.fileName} value={f.fileName}>\n                {f.routeId} · {f.routeDate} · {f.stopCount} stops\n              </option>\n            ))}\n          </select>\n          <button\n            onClick={runOptimize}\n            disabled={!selected || running}\n            className=\"bg-blue-600 hover:bg-blue-700 disabled:bg-gray-400 text-white text-sm font-medium px-4 py-1.5 rounded\"\n          >\n            {running ? (fixedSum!.duration ?? 0) - (freeSum!.duration ?? 0) : null;\n\n  return (\n    <>\n      <section className=\"bg-white border rounded-lg p-4\">\n        <h2 className=\"text-lg font-semibold\">\n          Route {route.routeId} · {route.routeDate}\n        </h2>\n        <p className=\"text-sm text-gray-600 mt-1\">\n          Depot {route.depot.name} ({route.depot.lat.toFixed(5)}, {route.depot.lng.toFixed(5)}) · {route.stops.length} stops\n          {route.vehicleStartSec != null && <> · shift {fmtTime(route.vehicleStartSec)}–{fmtTime(route.vehicleEndSec ?? undefined)}</>}\n        </p>\n        {bothDone && (\n          <p className=\"mt-2 text-sm\">\n            <span className=\"font-medium\">NextBillion vs planned:</span>{\" \"}\n            <span className={distSaved! >= 0 ? \"text-green-700\" : \"text-red-700\"}>\n              {distSaved! >= 0 ? \"−\" : \"+\"}{fmtKm(Math.abs(distSaved!))} distance\n            </span>{\" · \"}\n            <span className={durSaved! >= 0 ? \"text-green-700\" : \"text-red-700\"}>\n              {durSaved! >= 0 ? \"−\" : \"+\"}{fmtMin(Math.abs(durSaved!))} time\n            </span>\n          </p>\n        )}\n      </section>\n      <section className=\"grid grid-cols-1 md:grid-cols-2 gap-4\">\n        <SideCard title=\"Planned sequence (orden)\" side={fixed} stops={route.stops} />\n        <SideCard title=\"Optimized sequence (NextBillion)\" side={free} stops={route.stops} />\n      </section>\n    </>\n  );\n}\n\nfunction SideCard({ title, side, stops }: { title: string; side: SideState; stops: NormalizedStop[] }) {\n  const stopById = useMemo(() => {\n    const m = new Map<string, NormalizedStop>();\n    for (const s of stops) m.set(s.id, s);\n    return m;\n  }, [stops]);\n\n  const route = side.result?.routes?.[0];\n  const summary = side.result?.summary;\n  const unassigned = side.result?.unassigned ?? \"\");\n              return <li key={i}><span className=\"font-medium\">{stop?.name ?? u.id}</span>{u.reason && <span className=\"text-gray-500\"> — {u.reason}</span>}</li>;\n            })}\n          </ul>\n        </details>\n      )}\n      {route && (\n        <div className=\"mt-3 overflow-x-auto\">\n          <table className=\"w-full text-sm\">\n            <thead className=\"bg-gray-100 text-gray-700\">\n              <tr>\n                <th className=\"text-left p-2\">#</th>\n                <th className=\"text-left p-2\">Stop</th>\n                <th className=\"text-left p-2\">Arrival</th>\n                <th className=\"text-left p-2\">Planned</th>\n              </tr>\n            </thead>\n            <tbody>\n              {route.steps.map((step, i) => {\n                const stop = stopById.get(stopIdFromJob(step.id) ?? \"\");\n                const isJob = step.type === \"job\" || step.type === \"pickup\" || step.type === \"delivery\";\n                return (\n                  <tr key={i} className=\"border-b last:border-b-0\">\n                    <td className=\"p-2 font-mono text-gray-500\">{i}</td>\n                    <td className=\"p-2\">\n                      {step.type === \"start\" && <span className=\"text-green-700\">▶ depot start</span>}\n                      {step.type === \"end\" && <span className=\"text-red-700\">■ depot end</span>}\n                      {isJob && (\n                        <>\n                          <div className=\"font-medium\">{stop?.name ?? step.id ?? \"(job)\"} <span className=\"text-xs text-gray-400 font-mono\">{stop?.id}</span></div>\n                          {stop?.address && <div className=\"text-xs text-gray-500\">{stop.address}{stop.sector ? ` · ${stop.sector}` : \"\"}</div>}\n                        </>\n                      )}\n                    </td>\n                    <td className=\"p-2 font-mono text-xs\">{fmtTime(step.arrival)}</td>\n                    <td className=\"p-2 font-mono text-xs\">{isJob ? fmtTime(stop?.plannedTimeSec ?? undefined) : \"—\"}</td>\n                  </tr>\n                );\n              })}\n            </tbody>\n          </table>\n        </div>\n      )}\n    </div>\n  );\n}\n\nfunction StatusPill({ side, noFeasibleRoutes }: { side: SideState; noFeasibleRoutes?: boolean }) {\n  if (side.status === \"done\") {\n    if (noFeasibleRoutes) return <span className=\"text-xs px-2 py-0.5 rounded-full bg-amber-100 text-amber-800\">no feasible routes</span>;\n    return <span className=\"text-xs px-2 py-0.5 rounded-full bg-green-100 text-green-800\">done</span>;\n  }\n  if (side.status === \"error\") return <span className=\"text-xs px-2 py-0.5 rounded-full bg-red-100 text-red-800\">error</span>;\n  if (side.status === \"polling\") return <span className=\"text-xs px-2 py-0.5 rounded-full bg-blue-100 text-blue-800\">polling… (#{side.attempts})</span>;\n  if (side.status === \"submitting\") return <span className=\"text-xs px-2 py-0.5 rounded-full bg-blue-100 text-blue-800\">submitting…</span>;\n  return null;\n}\n"
}

 "file_path": "/Users/[USER]/workspace/poc_data/CARGO_EXPRESO/demo/src/lib/nb-optimize.ts",
 "content": "const NB_OPTIMIZE_URL = \"https://api.nextbillion.io/optimization/v2\";\nconst NB_RESULT_URL = \"https://api.nextbillion.io/optimization/v2/result\";\n\nexport interface NbSummary {\n  distanceM: number;\n  durationSec: number;\n  serviceSec: number;\n  jobs: number;\n  unassigned: number;\n}\n\nexport async function submit(body: unknown, apiKey: string): Promise<string> {\n  const r = await fetch(`${NB_OPTIMIZE_URL}?key=${encodeURIComponent(apiKey)}`, {\n    method: \"POST\",\n    headers: { \"Content-Type\": \"application/json\" },\n    body: JSON.stringify(body),\n  });\n  const text = await r.text();\n  if (!r.ok) throw new Error(`NB submit ${r.status}: ${text.slice(0, 200)}`);\n  const data = JSON.parse(text);\n  if (!data.id) throw new Error(`No id in NB response: ${text.slice(0, 200)}`);\n  return data.id as string;\n}\n\n// Poll a submitted job until it produces routes/unassigned/summary, or throw.\nexport async function pollResult(\n  id: string,\n  apiKey: string,\n  opts: { intervalMs?: number; maxAttempts?: number } = {}\n): Promise<Record<string, unknown>> {\n  const intervalMs = opts.intervalMs ?? 3000;\n  const maxAttempts = opts.maxAttempts ?? 80;\n  for (let i = 0; i < maxAttempts; i++) {\n    const r = await fetch(`${NB_RESULT_URL}?id=${encodeURIComponent(id)}&key=${encodeURIComponent(apiKey)}`);\n    const text = await r.text();\n    let data: Record<string, unknown> & { result?: Record<string, unknown> };\n    try {\n      data = JSON.parse(text);\n    } catch {\n      throw new Error(`non-JSON from NB (${r.status}): ${text.slice(0, 160)}`);\n    }\n    const top = String(data?.status ?? \"\").toLowerCase();\n    if (top === \"failed\" || top === \"error\" || data?.error) {\n      const err = data.error as { message?: string } | undefined;\n      throw new Error(err?.message ?? (data as { message?: string }).message ?? \"optimization failed\");\n    }\n    const result = (data.result ?? data) as Record<string, unknown>;\n    if (Array.isArray(result?.routes) || Array.isArray(result?.unassigned) || result?.summary != null) {\n      return result;\n    }\n    await new Promise((res) => setTimeout(res, intervalMs));\n  }\n  throw new Error(`timed out polling id ${id}`);\n}\n\n// Submit a body and poll to completion.\nexport async function solve(body: unknown, apiKey: string): Promise<Record<string, unknown>> {\n  const id = await submit(body, apiKey);\n  return pollResult(id, apiKey);\n}\n\nexport function extractSummary(result: Record<string, unknown>): NbSummary {\n  const summary = (result?.summary ?? {}) as Record<string, number>;\n  const routes = (result?.routes ?? []) as Array<{ steps?: Array<{ type?: string }> }>;\n  const jobs = routes.reduce(\n    (n, rt) => n + (rt.steps ?? []).filter((s) => s.type === \"job\" || s.type === \"pickup\" || s.type === \"delivery\").length,\n    0\n  );\n  const unassigned = Array.isArray(result?.unassigned) ? (result.unassigned as unknown[]).length : 0;\n  return {\n    distanceM: Number(summary.distance ?? 0),\n    durationSec: Number(summary.duration ?? 0),\n    serviceSec: Number(summary.service ?? 0),\n    jobs,\n    unassigned,\n  };\n}\n"
}

 "content": "import * as XLSX from \"xlsx\";\nimport { listRouteFiles, loadNormalizedRoute } from \"@/lib/data\";\nimport { buildOptimizationInput } from \"@/lib/nb-input\";\nimport { solve, extractSummary, type NbSummary } from \"@/lib/nb-optimize\";\n\n// Run up to this many routes concurrently (each route = 2 NB jobs).\nconst CONCURRENCY = 4;\n\ninterface RowResult {\n  routeId: string;\n  stops: number;\n  planned?: NbSummary;\n  optimized?: NbSummary;\n  error?: string;\n}\n\nasync function compareRoute(fileName: string, apiKey: string): Promise<RowResult> {\n  const route = loadNormalizedRoute(fileName);\n  if (!route) return { routeId: fileName, stops: 0, error: \"route not found\" };\n  try {\n    const fixed = buildOptimizationInput(route, \"fixed\");\n    const free = buildOptimizationInput(route, \"free\");\n    const [plannedRes, optRes] = await Promise.all([\n      solve(fixed.body, apiKey),\n      solve(free.body, apiKey),\n    ]);\n    return {\n      routeId: route.routeId,\n      stops: route.stops.length,\n      planned: extractSummary(plannedRes),\n      optimized: extractSummary(optRes),\n    };\n  } catch (e) {\n    return { routeId: route.routeId, stops: route.stops.length, error: e instanceof Error ? e.message : String(e) };\n  }\n}\n\nasync function runPool<T, R>(items: T[], worker: (item: T) => Promise<R>, concurrency: number): Promise<R[]> {\n  const results = new Array<R>(items.length);\n  let idx = 0;\n  const runners = Array.from({ length: Math.min(concurrency, items.length) }, async () => {\n    while (idx < items.length) {\n      const i = idx++;\n      results[i] = await worker(items[i]);\n    }\n  });\n  await Promise.all(runners);\n  return results;\n}\n\nconst km = (m?: number) => (m == null ? null : +(m / 1000).toFixed(2));\nconst min = (s?: number) => (s == null ? null : Math.round(s / 60));\nconst pct = (a?: number, b?: number) =>\n  a == null || b == null || a === 0 ? null : +(((a - b) / a) * 100).toFixed(1);\n\nexport async function POST() {\n  const apiKey = process.env.NB_API_KEY;\n  if (!apiKey || apiKey === \"your_api_key_here\") {\n    return Response.json({ error: \"NB_API_KEY not configured (.env.local)\" }, { status: 500 });\n  }\n\n  const files = listRouteFiles();\n  if (files.length === 0) return Response.json({ error: \"no routes found\" }, { status: 400 });\n\n  const rows = await runPool(files.map((f) => f.fileName), (f) => compareRoute(f, apiKey), CONCURRENCY);\n\n  // Build the Summary sheet.\n  const header = [\n    \"ROUTE\", \"STOPS\",\n    \"PLANNED_DIST_KM\", \"PLANNED_TIME_MIN\",\n    \"OPT_DIST_KM\", \"OPT_TIME_MIN\",\n    \"DIST_SAVED_KM\", \"DIST_SAVED_%\",\n    \"TIME_SAVED_MIN\", \"TIME_SAVED_%\",\n    \"PLANNED_UNASSIGNED\", \"OPT_UNASSIGNED\", \"NOTE\",\n  ];\n  const aoa: (string | number | null)[][] = [header];\n  let totPlannedM = 0, totOptM = 0, totPlannedS = 0, totOptS = 0;\n  for (const r of rows) {\n    if (r.error) {\n      aoa.push([r.routeId, r.stops, null, null, null, null, null, null, null, null, null, null, `ERROR: ${r.error}`]);\n      continue;\n    }\n    const p = r.planned!, o = r.optimized!;\n    totPlannedM += p.distanceM; totOptM += o.distanceM;\n    totPlannedS += p.durationSec; totOptS += o.durationSec;\n    aoa.push([\n      r.routeId, r.stops,\n      km(p.distanceM), min(p.durationSec),\n      km(o.distanceM), min(o.durationSec),\n      km(p.distanceM - o.distanceM), pct(p.distanceM, o.distanceM),\n      min(p.durationSec - o.durationSec), pct(p.durationSec, o.durationSec),\n      p.unassigned, o.unassigned, \"\",\n    ]);\n  }\n  // Totals row.\n  aoa.push([\n    \"TOTAL\", rows.reduce((n, r) => n + (r.error ? 0 : r.stops), 0),\n    km(totPlannedM), min(totPlannedS),\n    km(totOptM), min(totOptS),\n    km(totPlannedM - totOptM), pct(totPlannedM, totOptM),\n    min(totPlannedS - totOptS), pct(totPlannedS, totOptS),\n    null, null, \"\",\n  ]);\n\n  const ws = XLSX.utils.aoa_to_sheet(aoa);\n  ws[\"!cols\"] = header.map((h) => ({ wch: Math.max(12, h.length + 1) }));\n  const wb = XLSX.utils.book_new();\n  XLSX.utils.book_append_sheet(wb, ws, \"Route Comparison\");\n  const buf = XLSX.write(wb, { type: \"buffer\", bookType: \"xlsx\" }) as Buffer;\n\n  return new Response(new Uint8Array(buf), {\n    status: 200,\n    headers: {\n      \"Content-Type\": \"application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet\",\n      \"Content-Disposition\": `attachment; filename=\"cargo_expreso_route_comparison.xlsx\"`,\n    },\n  });\n}\n"
}

### CLAUDE (2026-07-15T22:30:32.124Z)

The Cargo Expreso demo is built, working, and verified end-to-end.

## What was built

A Next.js demo in `CARGO_EXPRESO/demo/` mirroring the **GLWAS model** — a table-based side-by-side comparison per route (`RutaEntrega`):
- **Left: Planned sequence (`orden`)** — the original order, pinned via NextBillion's `in_direct_sequence` relation.
- **Right: Optimized sequence (NextBillion)** — the same stops, order chosen by the optimizer.

**Data:** `scripts/build-routes.mjs` converts the spreadsheet into 21 per-route JSON files (1,388 stops) under `data/routes/`, depot from `ne-xt_depots.csv`.

**Your four requests, all applied and verified live:**
- ✅ **08:00 departure** — every route leaves the depot at 08:00 local (America/Guatemala). Confirmed: start step arrival = 08:00.
- ✅ **5-min service** per stop (was 2). Confirmed: `service: 300`.
- ✅ **"Run all → Excel" button** — POSTs to a new `/api/optimize/all` endpoint that optimizes all 21 routes (concurrency 4) and streams back `cargo_expreso_route_comparison.xlsx`.

**The Excel** (generated in ~35s) has a row per route + TOTAL: planned vs optimized distance/time, km & % saved, and unassigned counts. Result across all routes: **878 km planned → 569 km optimized (−35% distance, −42% time)**, with **0 stops dropped anywhere**.

**One bug I caught and fixed during testing:** the initial 10-hour shift made large routes (120–136 stops × 5-min service ≈ 10–11 h of service alone) infeasible for the forced sequence — NB dropped all stops, showing 0 km planned. I widened the shift so no stops drop for time reasons (it's a sequence-efficiency comparison, not a shift-compliance test), and re-verified every route now places all stops.

## To run it

```bash
cd CARGO_EXPRESO/demo
cp .env.local.example .env.local   # set NB_API_KEY  (I put a working key in .env.local for testing — git-ignored)
npm install
npm run dev                        # http://localhost:3000
```

I also added a `README.md` and a `Dockerfile` (with `CARGO_DATA_DIR`, `output: standalone`) so it deploys the same way as GLWAS.

Two notes: I skipped the login/auth layer GLWAS has (say the word and I'll port the middleware + login page). And the demo currently has **no map** — that matches GLWAS, which is table-only; if you'd like an actual map view of the two routes, that's a straightforward add.

The spec is clear. Key semantics:
- **`options.grouping.order_grouping.grouping_diameter`** (meters, straight-line **diameter**) — groups nearby tasks into one stop with no inter-task travel cost, and **only one setup time** (the max) is charged per group; service still applies per task.
- **`job.setup`** (seconds) — one-time per task **location**, not repeated for multiple tasks at the same spot.

### CLAUDE (2026-07-15T22:39:14.016Z)

All three changes are applied, verified live, and the batch Excel still generates cleanly (0 stops dropped, all 21 routes valid).

## Changes to `src/lib/nb-input.ts` (both fixed and free runs share this builder)

1. **Order grouping, 250 m radius** — added `options.grouping.order_grouping.grouping_diameter`. NB's field is a *diameter*, so `grouping_diameter = 500` (= 2 × 250 m radius). Grouped orders are treated as one stop: no inter-order travel cost and a single shared setup.
2. **Service time → 0** for every order.
3. **Setup time → 5 min (300 s)** per order — charged once per stop-location/group.

## Verified live (D0R42, 37 orders)
- `service: 0` ✓
- `setup: 900 s` = **3 × 300 s** — the 37 orders collapsed into **3 groups** within the 250 m radius, each charged one 5-min setup (vs 37 × 5 min without grouping). Grouping is clearly working.
- Distances dropped meaningfully now that intra-group travel is free — full-fleet total went from 878 → **644 km planned**, **429 km optimized (−33.5%)**, still 0 stops dropped.

## UI
The third summary metric per side now shows **Setup** (service would just read 0), and I added `setup` to the result type. README model notes updated.

One thing to flag on the "250 m radius" reading: I interpreted it geometrically as a radius, so `grouping_diameter = 500 m`. If you actually meant the grouping *distance* (max separation between grouped orders) to be 250 m, change `GROUPING_RADIUS_M` → set the diameter to 250 directly — it's a single labeled constant at the top of `nb-input.ts`. (The largest routes carry ~11 h of service alone.)\nconst SHIFT_LENGTH_SEC = 24 * 3600;\n// Guatemala is America/Guatemala = UTC-6 year-round (no DST).\nconst GT_OFFSET_SEC = -6 * 3600;\n\n// 08:00 local on the route's calendar date, as a unix timestamp.\nfunction departureSec(routeDate: string): number {\n  const [y, mo, d] = routeDate.split(\"-\").map(Number);\n  if (!y || !mo || !d) return Math.floor(Date.now() / 1000);\n  return Math.round(Date.UTC(y, mo - 1, d, DEPARTURE_HOUR_LOCAL, 0, 0) / 1000) - GT_OFFSET_SEC;\n}",
 "new_string": "// Every route runs an 08:00–17:00 local shift on its route date.\nconst SHIFT_START_HOUR = 8;\nconst SHIFT_END_HOUR = 17;\n// Guatemala is America/Guatemala = UTC-6 year-round (no DST).\nconst GT_OFFSET_SEC = -6 * 3600;\n\n// A given local hour on the route's calendar date, as a unix timestamp.\nfunction localHourSec(routeDate: string, hour: number): number {\n  const [y, mo, d] = routeDate.split(\"-\").map(Number);\n  if (!y || !mo || !d) return Math.floor(Date.now() / 1000) + hour * 3600;\n  return Math.round(Date.UTC(y, mo - 1, d, hour, 0, 0) / 1000) - GT_OFFSET_SEC;\n}\n\n// The vehicle shift window [start, end] for a route date — the single source of\n// truth used for both the optimization request and the UI display.\nexport function shiftWindow(routeDate: string): { startSec: number; endSec: number } {\n  return {\n    startSec: localHourSec(routeDate, SHIFT_START_HOUR),\n    endSec: localHourSec(routeDate, SHIFT_END_HOUR),\n  };\n}"

  poll "$FID" "PLANNED"
  poll "$FREEID" "OPT"
}

The 2 h overtime **rescues the borderline routes** (e.g. D0132 planned, which previously ran to 16:35). But **D0105's planned route is still infeasible** — with traffic on, its original `orden` sequence needs **more than 11 hours** (08:00 + service/setup + a very inefficient zigzag), so even +2 h can't fit it. Its **optimized** run finishes comfortably by **14:19**. That's actually the demo's strongest data point: the planned route literally can't be driven in a shift-plus-overtime, but reordering makes it fit. The Excel flags that one row (`infeasible even with overtime …`) and excludes it from the fleet totals rather than showing a misleading 0.

 "content": "#!/usr/bin/env node\n/**\n * Build per-(ROUTE, DATE) JSON files for the DHL PL demo from the source\n * spreadsheet. ROUTE is the vehicle id; stops are grouped by DATE and ordered by\n * TIME START (the planned sequence).\n *\n *   cd DHL_PL/demo && npm run build-routes\n *\n * Reads   ../data/Plik 1 Daily test.xlsx  (sheets \"Zlecenia\" and \"Depot\")\n * Writes  ./data/routes/<ROUTE>__<DATE>.json\n */\nimport fs from \"node:fs\";\nimport path from \"node:path\";\nimport { fileURLToPath } from \"node:url\";\nimport XLSX from \"xlsx\";\n\nconst __dirname = path.dirname(fileURLToPath(import.meta.url));\nconst SRC = path.resolve(__dirname, \"..\", \"..\", \"data\");\nconst OUT = path.resolve(__dirname, \"..\", \"data\", \"routes\");\nconst XLSX_FILE = path.join(SRC, \"Plik 1 Daily test.xlsx\");\n\n// Time/date fields are read as xlsx raw:false strings for deterministic parsing.\n// Durations are \"H:MM[:SS]\"; datetimes are \"M/D/YY H:MM[:SS]\" in Europe/Warsaw.\nfunction durationSeconds(cell) {\n  if (cell == null || cell === \"\") return 0;\n  const m = String(cell).match(/(\\d+):(\\d+)(?::(\\d+))?/);\n  return m ? +m[1] * 3600 + +m[2] * 60 + +(m[3] || 0) : 0;\n}\nconst WARSAW_FMT = new Intl.DateTimeFormat(\"en-US\", {\n  timeZone: \"Europe/Warsaw\", year: \"numeric\", month: \"2-digit\", day: \"2-digit\",\n  hour: \"2-digit\", minute: \"2-digit\", second: \"2-digit\", hour12: false,\n});\n// Warsaw wall-clock -> true unix epoch (seconds), DST-aware.\nfunction warsawEpoch(y, mo, d, h, mi, s) {\n  const asUtc = Date.UTC(y, mo - 1, d, h, mi, s);\n  const p = Object.fromEntries(\n    WARSAW_FMT.formatToParts(new Date(asUtc)).filter((x) => x.type !== \"literal\").map((x) => [x.type, +x.value])\n  );\n  const shown = Date.UTC(p.year, p.month - 1, p.day, p.hour % 24, p.minute, p.second);\n  return Math.round(asUtc / 1000) - (shown - asUtc) / 1000;\n}\nfunction parseWarsawDateTime(str) {\n  if (!str) return null;\n  const m = String(str).match(/(\\d+)\\/(\\d+)\\/(\\d+)\\s+(\\d+):(\\d+)(?::(\\d+))?/);\n  if (!m) return null;\n  const yy = +m[3];\n  return warsawEpoch(yy < 100 ? 2000 + yy : yy, +m[1], +m[2], +m[4], +m[5], +(m[6] || 0));\n}\nfunction dateKey(str) {\n  const m = String(str).match(/(\\d+)\\/(\\d+)\\/(\\d+)/);\n  if (!m) return String(str).slice(0, 10);\n  const yy = +m[3], y = yy < 100 ? 2000 + yy : yy;\n  return `${y}-${String(+m[1]).padStart(2, \"0\")}-${String(+m[2]).padStart(2, \"0\")}`;\n}\n\nfunction readDepot(wb) {\n  const dep = XLSX.utils.sheet_to_json(wb.Sheets[\"Depot\"], { raw: true, defval: null });\n  const r = dep.find((x) => x[\"Longitude X\"] != null && x[\"Latitude Y\"] != null);\n  if (!r) throw new Error(\"Depot sheet: no row with Longitude X / Latitude Y\");\n  return { name: String(r.Depot ?? \"DEPOT\").trim(), lat: +r[\"Latitude Y\"], lng: +r[\"Longitude X\"] };\n}\n\nfunction main() {\n  const wb = XLSX.read(fs.readFileSync(XLSX_FILE));\n  const num = XLSX.utils.sheet_to_json(wb.Sheets[\"Zlecenia\"], { raw: true, defval: null });\n  const fmt = XLSX.utils.sheet_to_json(wb.Sheets[\"Zlecenia\"], { raw: false, defval: null });\n  const depot = readDepot(wb);\n\n  const groups = new Map(); // \"route|date\" -> {routeId, routeDate, stops[]}\n  for (let i = 0; i < num.length; i++) {\n    const r = num[i], f = fmt[i];\n    if (r.X == null || r.Y == null || r.ROUTE == null || f.DATE == null) continue;\n    const route = String(r.ROUTE).trim();\n    const date = dateKey(f.DATE);\n    const key = `${route}|${date}`;\n    if (!groups.has(key)) groups.set(key, { routeId: route, routeDate: date, stops: [] });\n    const a = parseWarsawDateTime(f[\"TIME START\"]);\n    const b = parseWarsawDateTime(f[\"TIME STOP\"]);\n    groups.get(key).stops.push({\n      id: String(r.ID),\n      type: String(r.TYPE ?? \"\").toLowerCase(),\n      name: String(r.NAME ?? \"\").trim(),\n      address: [r.STREET, r[\"NUMBER STREET\"], r.CITY].map((x) => String(x ?? \"\").trim()).filter(Boolean).join(\", \"),\n      lat: +r.Y,\n      lng: +r.X,\n      service: durationSeconds(f[\"TIME FOR STOP\"]),\n      windowStartSec: a,\n      windowEndSec: b != null && a != null && b > a ? b : null,\n      fileOrder: i,\n    });\n  }\n\n  fs.mkdirSync(OUT, { recursive: true });\n  for (const f of fs.readdirSync(OUT)) if (f.endsWith(\".json\")) fs.unlinkSync(path.join(OUT, f));\n\n  let total = 0;\n  for (const [, g] of [...groups.entries()].sort()) {\n    // Planned sequence = ordered by TIME START, ties broken by file order.\n    g.stops.sort((x, y) => (x.windowStartSec ?? 0) - (y.windowStartSec ?? 0) || x.fileOrder - y.fileOrder);\n    g.stops.forEach((s, seq) => { s.sequence = seq + 1; delete s.fileOrder; });\n    const out = { routeId: g.routeId, routeDate: g.routeDate, depot, stops: g.stops };\n    fs.writeFileSync(path.join(OUT, `${g.routeId}__${g.routeDate}.json`), JSON.stringify(out, null, 2));\n    total += g.stops.length;\n  }\n\n  const routes = new Set([...groups.values()].map((g) => g.routeId));\n  const dates = new Set([...groups.values()].map((g) => g.routeDate));\n  console.log(`depot: ${depot.name} (${depot.lat}, ${depot.lng})`);\n  console.log(`wrote ${groups.size} route-day file(s): ${routes.size} routes x ${dates.size} dates, ${total} stops -> ${path.relative(process.cwd(), OUT)}`);\n}\n\nmain();\n"

 "content": "import fs from \"node:fs\";\nimport path from \"node:path\";\n\n// Container deployments set DHL_DATA_DIR to the bundled route JSON folder.\n// Local dev falls back to the generated ./data/routes directory.\nconst DATA_DIR =\n  process.env.DHL_DATA_DIR ?? path.join(process.cwd(), \"data\", \"routes\");\n\nexport interface RouteFileSummary {\n  fileName: string;\n  routeId: string; // ROUTE (vehicle id)\n  routeDate: string; // DATE (YYYY-MM-DD)\n  stopCount: number;\n}\n\nexport interface NormalizedStop {\n  id: string;\n  type: string; // delivery | pickup\n  sequence: number; // planned order (by TIME START)\n  name: string;\n  address: string;\n  lat: number;\n  lng: number;\n  service: number; // TIME FOR STOP, seconds\n  windowStartSec: number | null;\n  windowEndSec: number | null;\n}\n\nexport interface NormalizedRoute {\n  fileName: string;\n  routeId: string;\n  routeDate: string;\n  depot: { name: string; lat: number; lng: number };\n  stops: NormalizedStop[];\n}\n\nexport function listRouteFiles(): RouteFileSummary[] {\n  if (!fs.existsSync(DATA_DIR)) return [];\n  const out: RouteFileSummary[] = [];\n  for (const fileName of fs.readdirSync(DATA_DIR).sort()) {\n    if (!fileName.endsWith(\".json\")) continue;\n    try {\n      const data = JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync(path.join(DATA_DIR, fileName), \"utf-8\"));\n      out.push({\n        fileName,\n        routeId: String(data.routeId ?? \"\"),\n        routeDate: String(data.routeDate ?? \"\"),\n        stopCount: (data.stops ?? []).length,\n      });\n    } catch {\n      // skip unparseable files\n    }\n  }\n  return out;\n}\n\nexport function loadNormalizedRoute(fileName: string): NormalizedRoute | null {\n  // Guard against path traversal: only accept a bare basename.\n  if (fileName !== path.basename(fileName) || !fileName.endsWith(\".json\")) return null;\n  const full = path.join(DATA_DIR, fileName);\n  if (!fs.existsSync(full)) return null;\n  const data = JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync(full, \"utf-8\"));\n  const stops: NormalizedStop[] = (data.stops ?? [])\n    .filter((s: { lat: number; lng: number }) => Number.isFinite(s.lat) && Number.isFinite(s.lng))\n    .map((s: NormalizedStop) => ({\n      id: String(s.id),\n      type: String(s.type ?? \"\"),\n      sequence: Number(s.sequence) || 0,\n      name: String(s.name ?? \"\"),\n      address: String(s.address ?? \"\"),\n      lat: Number(s.lat),\n      lng: Number(s.lng),\n      service: Number(s.service) || 0,\n      windowStartSec: s.windowStartSec != null ? Number(s.windowStartSec) : null,\n      windowEndSec: s.windowEndSec != null ? Number(s.windowEndSec) : null,\n    }))\n    .sort((a: NormalizedStop, b: NormalizedStop) => a.sequence - b.sequence);\n\n  return {\n    fileName,\n    routeId: String(data.routeId ?? \"\"),\n    routeDate: String(data.routeDate ?? \"\"),\n    depot: {\n      name: String(data.depot?.name ?? \"DEPOT\"),\n      lat: Number(data.depot?.lat),\n      lng: Number(data.depot?.lng),\n    },\n    stops,\n  };\n}\n"
}

 "file_path": "/Users/[USER]/workspace/poc_data/DHL_PL/demo/src/lib/nb-input.ts",
 "content": "import type { NormalizedRoute } from \"./data\";\n\n// Routing profile for all requests.\nexport const ROUTING_MODE = \"truck\";\n// Fallback shift bounds when a route has no declared time windows.\nconst DEFAULT_SHIFT_START_SEC = 8 * 3600;\nconst DEFAULT_SHIFT_LENGTH_SEC = 12 * 3600;\n\nexport interface BuiltInput {\n  body: Record<string, unknown>;\n  vehicleId: string;\n  jobIds: string[];\n}\n\n// The vehicle shift window for a route: spans every stop's time window (so the\n// planned/optimized routes have room to run), with a generous fallback.\nexport function shiftWindow(route: NormalizedRoute): { startSec: number; endSec: number } {\n  let start = Infinity, end = -Infinity;\n  for (const s of route.stops) {\n    if (s.windowStartSec != null) start = Math.min(start, s.windowStartSec);\n    if (s.windowEndSec != null) end = Math.max(end, s.windowEndSec);\n  }\n  if (!Number.isFinite(start)) {\n    const base = Math.floor(Date.parse(route.routeDate) / 1000) + DEFAULT_SHIFT_START_SEC;\n    return { startSec: base, endSec: base + DEFAULT_SHIFT_LENGTH_SEC };\n  }\n  if (!Number.isFinite(end)) end = start + DEFAULT_SHIFT_LENGTH_SEC;\n  return { startSec: start, endSec: end };\n}\n\n/**\n * Build a NextBillion.ai Optimization v2 input body for a single (ROUTE, DATE).\n * @param mode \"fixed\" forces the planned TIME START order via an\n *             in_direct_sequence relation (timing unconstrained); \"free\" lets\n *             the optimizer choose the order and honors each stop's time window.\n */\nexport function buildOptimizationInput(route: NormalizedRoute, mode: \"fixed\" | \"free\"): BuiltInput {\n  const { startSec, endSec } = shiftWindow(route);\n\n  // 0: depot, 1..N: stops in planned (TIME START) order.\n  const locationStrings: string[] = [`${route.depot.lat},${route.depot.lng}`];\n  const jobIds: string[] = [];\n  const jobs: Array<Record<string, unknown>> = [];\n\n  for (const stop of route.stops) {\n    const idx = locationStrings.length;\n    locationStrings.push(`${stop.lat},${stop.lng}`);\n    const jobId = `job_${stop.id}_${idx}`; // unique even if an ID repeats\n    jobIds.push(jobId);\n    const job: Record<string, unknown> = {\n      id: jobId,\n      description: stop.name || stop.id,\n      location_index: idx,\n      service: stop.service,\n    };\n    // Free mode honors per-stop time windows; fixed mode ignores them so the\n    // forced sequence stays feasible regardless of window timing.\n    if (mode === \"free\" && stop.windowStartSec != null && stop.windowEndSec != null) {\n      job.time_windows = [[stop.windowStartSec, stop.windowEndSec]];\n    }\n    jobs.push(job);\n  }\n\n  const vehicleId = `veh_${route.routeId}_${route.routeDate}`;\n  const vehicle: Record<string, unknown> = {\n    id: vehicleId,\n    start_index: 0,\n    end_index: 0,\n    time_window: [startSec, endSec],\n  };\n\n  const body: Record<string, unknown> = {\n    description: `${route.routeId} ${route.routeDate} (${mode})`,\n    options: { routing: { mode: ROUTING_MODE } },\n    locations: { id: 1, location: locationStrings },\n    jobs,\n    vehicles: [vehicle],\n  };\n\n  if (mode === \"fixed\" && jobIds.length > 0) {\n    body.relations = [\n      {\n        type: \"in_direct_sequence\",\n        vehicle: vehicleId,\n        steps: [{ type: \"start\" }, ...jobIds.map((id) => ({ type: \"job\", id })), { type: \"end\" }],\n      },\n    ];\n  }\n\n  return { body, vehicleId, jobIds };\n}\n"
}

e.message : String(e) };\n  }\n}\n\nasync function runPool<T, R>(items: T[], worker: (item: T) => Promise<R>, concurrency: number): Promise<R[]> {\n  const results = new Array<R>(items.length);\n  let idx = 0;\n  const runners = Array.from({ length: Math.min(concurrency, items.length) }, async () => {\n    while (idx < items.length) {\n      const i = idx++;\n      results[i] = await worker(items[i]);\n    }\n  });\n  await Promise.all(runners);\n  return results;\n}\n\nconst km = (m?: number) => (m == null ? \"\" : `unassigned (planned ${p.unassigned}, optimized ${o.unassigned})`;\n    aoa.push([\n      r.routeId, r.routeDate, r.stops,\n      km(p.distanceM), min(p.durationSec),\n      km(o.distanceM), min(o.durationSec),\n      comparable ? 0 : r.stops), 0),\n    km(totPlannedM), min(totPlannedS), km(totOptM), min(totOptS),\n    km(totPlannedM - totOptM), pct(totPlannedM, totOptM),\n    min(totPlannedS - totOptS), pct(totPlannedS, totOptS),\n    null, null, \"\",\n  ]);\n\n  const ws = XLSX.utils.aoa_to_sheet(aoa);\n  ws[\"!cols\"] = header.map((h) => ({ wch: Math.max(11, h.length + 1) }));\n  const wb = XLSX.utils.book_new();\n  XLSX.utils.book_append_sheet(wb, ws, \"Route Comparison\");\n  const buf = XLSX.write(wb, { type: \"buffer\", bookType: \"xlsx\" }) as Buffer;\n\n  return new Response(new Uint8Array(buf), {\n    status: 200,\n    headers: {\n      \"Content-Type\": \"application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet\",\n      \"Content-Disposition\": `attachment; filename=\"dhl_pl_route_comparison.xlsx\"`,\n    },\n  });\n}\n"

### CLAUDE (2026-07-16T13:10:22.841Z)

The DHL_PL demo is built, working, and verified live.

## What was built — `DHL_PL/demo/`

Same architecture as the CARGO_EXPRESO demo, adapted to the DHL `Plik 1 Daily test.xlsx` data:

- **`build-routes.mjs`** → 227 route-day JSON files (**47 routes × 5 dates, 29,435 stops**), keyed by `ROUTE` + `DATE`, stops ordered by `TIME START`, Warsaw-timezone parsing, depot from the `Depot` sheet.
- **UI flow you asked for:** select **Route** → then **Date** → **Run comparison**. Plus the **Run all → Excel** batch button.
- **Comparison:** left = **Planned (TIME START order)** pinned via `in_direct_sequence`; right = **Optimized (NextBillion)** which honors each stop's `TIME START`–`TIME STOP` window. Service = real `TIME FOR STOP`, profile `truck`.
- API routes (`/api/routes`, `/api/optimize`, `/api/optimize/result`, `/api/optimize/all`), README, and a `Dockerfile` (`DHL_DATA_DIR`, standalone) mirroring CARGO/GLWAS.

## Verified live
- Routes API returns 227 route-days across 47 routes; Route→Date selection resolves correctly.
- Small route (PT_622, 15 stops): both sides feasible, orders genuinely differ.
- Large route (**PT_513 / 2026-06-17, 135 stops**): planned **1,335 km / 31 h** → optimized **225 km / 6.3 h**, 0 unassigned.

## One honest observation about the TIME START planned side
Because most deliveries share the **same 08:00 window**, ordering by `TIME START` leaves the tiebreak as file order — which isn't geographic — so the planned route zigzags badly (hence PT_513's 1,335 km). That makes the optimization gain look enormous. It's a truthful reflection of the ordering you chose, but if you'd rather the planned baseline be more realistic (e.g., a nearest-neighbor sequence, or genuinely respecting windows), that's a one-line change in `nb-input.ts` — let me know.

To run: `cd DHL_PL/demo && cp .env.local.example .env.local` (set `NB_API_KEY`), `npm install`, `npm run dev`. (I put a working key in the git-ignored `.env.local` for testing.) Note the **Run all → Excel** batch covers all 227 route-days (454 NB jobs) so it'll take several minutes — the poll budget is already set to 10 min/job.

\"free\" lets\n *             the optimizer choose the order and honors each stop's time window.\n */\nexport function buildOptimizationInput(route: NormalizedRoute, mode: \"fixed\" | \"free\"): BuiltInput {\n  const { startSec, endSec } = shiftWindow(route);\n\n  // 0: depot, 1..N: stops in planned (TIME START) order.\n  const locationStrings: string[] = [`${route.depot.lat},${route.depot.lng}`];\n  const jobIds: string[] = [];\n  const jobs: Array<Record<string, unknown>> = [];\n\n  for (const stop of route.stops) {\n    const idx = locationStrings.length;\n    locationStrings.push(`${stop.lat},${stop.lng}`);\n    const jobId = `job_${stop.id}_${idx}`; // unique even if an ID repeats\n    jobIds.push(jobId);\n    const job: Record<string, unknown> = {\n      id: jobId,\n      description: stop.name || stop.id,\n      location_index: idx,\n      service: stop.service,\n    };\n    // Free mode honors per-stop time windows; fixed mode ignores them so the\n    // forced sequence stays feasible regardless of window timing.\n    if (mode === \"free\" && stop.windowStartSec != null && stop.windowEndSec != null) {\n      job.time_windows = [[stop.windowStartSec, stop.windowEndSec]];\n    }\n    jobs.push(job);\n  }\n\n  const vehicleId = `veh_${route.routeId}_${route.routeDate}`;\n  const vehicle: Record<string, unknown> = {\n    id: vehicleId,\n    start_index: 0,\n    end_index: 0,\n    time_window: [startSec, endSec],\n  };\n\n  const body: Record<string, unknown> = {\n    description: `${route.routeId} ${route.routeDate} (${mode})`,\n    options: { routing: { mode: ROUTING_MODE } },\n    locations: { id: 1, location: locationStrings },\n    jobs,\n    vehicles: [vehicle],\n  };\n\n  if (mode === \"fixed\" && jobIds.length > 0) {\n    body.relations = [\n      {\n        type: \"in_direct_sequence\",\n        vehicle: vehicleId,\n        steps: [{ type: \"start\" }, ...jobIds.map((id) => ({ type: \"job\", id })), { type: \"end\" }],\n      },\n    ];\n  }\n\n  return { body, vehicleId, jobIds };\n}",
 "new_string": "/**\n * Build a NextBillion.ai Optimization v2 input body for a single (ROUTE, DATE).\n * The optimizer chooses the visit order and honors each stop's time window.\n */\nexport function buildOptimizationInput(route: NormalizedRoute): BuiltInput {\n  const { startSec, endSec } = shiftWindow(route);\n\n  // 0: depot, 1..N: the route's stops.\n  const locationStrings: string[] = [`${route.depot.lat},${route.depot.lng}`];\n  const jobIds: string[] = [];\n  const jobs: Array<Record<string, unknown>> = [];\n\n  for (const stop of route.stops) {\n    const idx = locationStrings.length;\n    locationStrings.push(`${stop.lat},${stop.lng}`);\n    const jobId = `job_${stop.id}_${idx}`; // unique even if an ID repeats\n    jobIds.push(jobId);\n    const job: Record<string, unknown> = {\n      id: jobId,\n      description: stop.name || stop.id,\n      location_index: idx,\n      service: stop.service,\n    };\n    if (stop.windowStartSec != null && stop.windowEndSec != null) {\n      job.time_windows = [[stop.windowStartSec, stop.windowEndSec]];\n    }\n    jobs.push(job);\n  }\n\n  const vehicleId = `veh_${route.routeId}_${route.routeDate}`;\n  const body: Record<string, unknown> = {\n    description: `${route.routeId} ${route.routeDate}`,\n    options: { routing: { mode: ROUTING_MODE } },\n    locations: { id: 1, location: locationStrings },\n    jobs,\n    vehicles: [{ id: vehicleId, start_index: 0, end_index: 0, time_window: [startSec, endSec] }],\n  };\n\n  return { body, vehicleId, jobIds };\n}"

 "content": "// Persist an optimization solution to the NextBillion console and build its\n// shareable console link, keyed by the optimization request_id.\n\nconst BFF_SAVE_URL = \"https://bff.nextbillion.ai/route-planner-api/v1/solutions:save\";\n\n// Console link for a saved/shared solution. `{request_id}` is substituted.\n// TODO: confirm this matches the exact URL from the console's Share button.\nconst SHARE_URL_TEMPLATE = \"https://console.nextbillion.ai/route-planner/{request_id}\";\n\nexport function shareUrl(requestId: string): string {\n  return SHARE_URL_TEMPLATE.replace(\"{request_id}\", encodeURIComponent(requestId));\n}\n\n/**\n * Save (share) the solution for `requestId` so its console link resolves.\n * Authorized with the ncc_token JWT (from NB_BFF_TOKEN). Returns true on success.\n */\nexport async function saveSolution(requestId: string, apiKey: string, bffToken: string): Promise<boolean> {\n  try {\n    const r = await fetch(`${BFF_SAVE_URL}?apiKey=${encodeURIComponent(apiKey)}`, {\n      method: \"POST\",\n      headers: {\n        \"content-type\": \"application/json\",\n        cookie: `ncc_token=[REDACTED]\n        Origin: \"https://console.nextbillion.ai\",\n        Referer: \"https://console.nextbillion.ai/\",\n      },\n      body: JSON.stringify({ request_id: requestId }),\n    });\n    return r.ok;\n  } catch {\n    return false;\n  }\n}\n"
