 "new_string": "// The vehicle shift window for a route: starts at 07:00 local (Europe/Warsaw)\n// on the route date and runs through the latest stop time window (with a\n// generous fallback when no windows are declared).\nexport function shiftWindow(route: NormalizedRoute): { startSec: number; endSec: number } {\n  const startSec = warsawHourSec(route.routeDate, SHIFT_START_HOUR_LOCAL);\n  let end = -Infinity;\n  for (const s of route.stops) if (s.windowEndSec != null) end = Math.max(end, s.windowEndSec);\n  const endSec = Number.isFinite(end) && end > startSec ? end : startSec + DEFAULT_SHIFT_LENGTH_SEC;\n  return { startSec, endSec };\n}"

Math.round(n) : 0; // already seconds\n}\nconst WARSAW_FMT = new Intl.DateTimeFormat(\"en-US\", {\n  timeZone: \"Europe/Warsaw\", year: \"numeric\", month: \"2-digit\", day: \"2-digit\",\n  hour: \"2-digit\", minute: \"2-digit\", second: \"2-digit\", hour12: false,\n});\nfunction warsawEpoch(y, mo, d, h, mi, s) {\n  const asUtc = Date.UTC(y, mo - 1, d, h, mi, s);\n  const p = Object.fromEntries(\n    WARSAW_FMT.formatToParts(new Date(asUtc)).filter((x) => x.type !== \"literal\").map((x) => [x.type, +x.value])\n  );\n  const shown = Date.UTC(p.year, p.month - 1, p.day, p.hour % 24, p.minute, p.second);\n  return Math.round(asUtc / 1000) - (shown - asUtc) / 1000;\n}\nfunction parseWarsawDateTime(str) {\n  if (!str) return null;\n  const m = String(str).match(/(\\d+)\\/(\\d+)\\/(\\d+)\\s+(\\d+):(\\d+)(?::(\\d+))?/);\n  if (!m) return null;\n  const yy = +m[3];\n  return warsawEpoch(yy < 100 ? 2000 + yy : yy, +m[1], +m[2], +m[4], +m[5], +(m[6] || 0));\n}\n\nfunction readDepots(wb) {\n  const rows = XLSX.utils.sheet_to_json(wb.Sheets[\"Dane DEPOT\"], { raw: true, defval: null });\n  const map = {};\n  for (const r of rows) {\n    const code = String(r.Depot ?? \"\").trim();\n    if (code && r[\"Longitude X\"] != null && r[\"Latitude Y\"] != null && Number.isFinite(+r[\"Longitude X\"])) {\n      map[code] = { name: code, address: String(r.Address ?? \"\").trim(), lat: +r[\"Latitude Y\"], lng: +r[\"Longitude X\"] };\n    }\n  }\n  return map;\n}\n\nfunction main() {\n  const wb = XLSX.read(fs.readFileSync(XLSX_FILE));\n  const depots = readDepots(wb);\n\n  fs.mkdirSync(OUT, { recursive: true });\n  for (const f of fs.readdirSync(OUT)) if (f.endsWith(\".json\")) fs.unlinkSync(path.join(OUT, f));\n\n  for (const { code, sheet } of TERMINALS) {\n    const num = XLSX.utils.sheet_to_json(wb.Sheets[sheet], { raw: true, defval: null });\n    const fmt = XLSX.utils.sheet_to_json(wb.Sheets[sheet], { raw: false, defval: null });\n    let excluded = 0;\n    const stops = [];\n    for (let i = 0; i < num.length; i++) {\n      const r = num[i], f = fmt[i];\n      const lat = +r.Y, lng = +r.X;\n      if (!Number.isFinite(lat) || !Number.isFinite(lng) || (lat === 0 && lng === 0)) { excluded++; continue; }\n      const type = String(r.TYPE ?? \"\").toLowerCase();\n      const pkgs = type === \"pickup\" ? (+r[\"PICKUP PACKAGES\"] || 0) : (+r[\"DELIVERY PACKAGES\"] || 0);\n      const weight = type === \"pickup\" ? (+r[\"PICKUP WEIGHT\"] || 0) : (+r[\"DELIVERY WEIGHT\"] || 0);\n      const a = parseWarsawDateTime(f[\"TIME FROM\"]);\n      const b = parseWarsawDateTime(f[\"TIME TO\"]);\n      stops.push({\n        id: String(r.ID),\n        type,\n        name: String(r.NAME ?? \"\").trim(),\n        address: [r.STREET, r[\"NUMBER STREET\"], r.CITY].map((x) => String(x ?? \"\").trim()).filter(Boolean).join(\", \"),\n        lat, lng,\n        // service = fixed stop time + per-package handling time.\n        service: durationSeconds(f[\"TIME FOR STOP\"]) + durationSeconds(f[\"TIME FOR PACKAGE\"]) * pkgs,\n        windowStartSec: a,\n        windowEndSec: b != null && a != null && b > a ? b : null,\n        weight: Math.round(weight),\n        parcels: pkgs,\n      });\n    }\n    const out = {\n      terminal: code,\n      depot: depots[code],\n      vehicle: { maxWeight: 1400, maxParcels: 500 },\n      targetRouteSeconds: 7 * 3600,\n      stops,\n    };\n    fs.writeFileSync(path.join(OUT, `${code}.json`), JSON.stringify(out));\n    console.log(`${code}: ${stops.length} stops (${excluded} excluded: null/0,0 coords), depot ${out.depot?.name} (${out.depot?.lat},${out.depot?.lng})`);\n  }\n}\n\nmain();\n"

 "content": "import type { Terminal } from \"./terminal-data\";\n\n// Routing profile for tactical planning.\nconst ROUTING_MODE = \"truck\";\n// Assume ~55% of a route's time is service when sizing the vehicle pool, then\n// pad — the objective minimizes the number actually used, so extra idle\n// vehicles are harmless; they only need to be an upper bound.\nconst SERVICE_FRACTION = 0.55;\nconst VEHICLE_BUFFER = 5;\n\nexport interface BuiltFleetInput {\n  body: Record<string, unknown>;\n  vehicleCount: number;\n}\n\n// Upper bound on the number of routes (vehicles) to offer the solver.\nfunction estimateVehicles(t: Terminal): number {\n  let serviceSec = 0, weight = 0, parcels = 0;\n  for (const s of t.stops) {\n    serviceSec += s.service;\n    if (s.type !== \"pickup\") { weight += s.weight; parcels += s.parcels; }\n  }\n  const byService = Math.ceil(serviceSec / (SERVICE_FRACTION * t.targetRouteSeconds));\n  const byWeight = Math.ceil(weight / t.vehicle.maxWeight);\n  const byParcels = Math.ceil(parcels / t.vehicle.maxParcels);\n  return Math.max(byService, byWeight, byParcels, 1) + VEHICLE_BUFFER;\n}\n\n/**\n * Build a NextBillion.ai Optimization v2 input for one terminal's tactical\n * fleet-sizing problem: serve every stop with routes of ~7 h, respecting the\n * vehicle payload/parcel limits, minimizing the number of routes used.\n */\nexport function buildFleetInput(t: Terminal): BuiltFleetInput {\n  // Shift window spans every stop's time window (fallback: a 14 h day).\n  let start = Infinity, end = -Infinity;\n  for (const s of t.stops) {\n    if (s.windowStartSec != null) start = Math.min(start, s.windowStartSec);\n    if (s.windowEndSec != null) end = Math.max(end, s.windowEndSec);\n  }\n  if (!Number.isFinite(start)) { start = 0; end = 14 * 3600; }\n  if (!Number.isFinite(end)) end = start + 14 * 3600;\n\n  const locationStrings: string[] = [`${t.depot.lat},${t.depot.lng}`];\n  const jobIds: string[] = [];\n  const jobs: Array<Record<string, unknown>> = [];\n  for (const s of t.stops) {\n    const idx = locationStrings.length;\n    locationStrings.push(`${s.lat},${s.lng}`);\n    const jobId = `job_${s.id}_${idx}`;\n    jobIds.push(jobId);\n    const job: Record<string, unknown> = {\n      id: jobId,\n      description: s.name || s.id,\n      location_index: idx,\n      service: s.service,\n    };\n    if (s.windowStartSec != null && s.windowEndSec != null) job.time_windows = [[s.windowStartSec, s.windowEndSec]];\n    const amount = [s.weight, s.parcels];\n    if (s.type === \"pickup\") job.pickup = amount; else job.delivery = amount;\n    jobs.push(job);\n  }\n\n  const vehicleCount = estimateVehicles(t);\n  const vehicles = Array.from({ length: vehicleCount }, (_, i) => ({\n    id: `veh_${t.terminal}_${i + 1}`,\n    start_index: 0,\n    end_index: 0,\n    time_window: [start, end],\n    capacity: [t.vehicle.maxWeight, t.vehicle.maxParcels],\n    max_working_time: t.targetRouteSeconds, // ~7 h cap (service + drive + wait)\n  }));\n\n  const body: Record<string, unknown> = {\n    description: `${t.terminal} tactical fleet sizing`,\n    options: {\n      routing: { mode: ROUTING_MODE },\n      // Minimize the number of routes used, then travel time.\n      objective: { travel_cost: \"duration\", custom: { type: \"min\", value: \"vehicles\" } },\n    },\n    locations: { id: 1, location: locationStrings },\n    jobs,\n    vehicles,\n  };\n\n  return { body, vehicleCount };\n}\n"
}

Determine the number of routes required to serve every stop for a terminal, targeting ~7&nbsp;h routes\n          within the {info?.vehicle.maxWeight ?? 1400}&nbsp;kg / {info?.vehicle.maxParcels ??  "content": "import * as XLSX from \"xlsx\";\nimport { listTerminals, loadTerminal } from \"@/lib/terminal-data\";\nimport { buildFleetInput } from \"@/lib/plik2-input\";\nimport { solve } from \"@/lib/nb-optimize\";\n\ninterface NbRoute {\n  vehicle: string;\n  steps?: Array<{ type?: string }>;\n  distance?: number;\n  duration?: number;\n  delivery?: number[];\n  pickup?: number[];\n}\n\nconst hms = (sec?: number) => {\n  if (sec == null) return null;\n  const s = Math.max(0, Math.round(sec));\n  const p = (n: number) => String(n).padStart(2, \"0\");\n  return `${p(Math.floor(s / 3600))}:${p(Math.floor((s % 3600) / 60))}:${p(s % 60)}`;\n};\nconst km = (m?: number) => (m == null ? null : +(m / 1000).toFixed(2));\n\nasync function solveTerminal(code: string, apiKey: string) {\n  const terminal = loadTerminal(code);\n  if (!terminal) return { code, error: \"not found\" };\n  try {\n    const built = buildFleetInput(terminal);\n    const res = (await solve(built.body, apiKey)) as { routes?: NbRoute[]; unassigned?: unknown[] };\n    return { code, terminal, routes: res.routes ?? [], unassigned: (res.unassigned ?? []).length };\n  } catch (e) {\n    return { code, error: e instanceof Error ? e.message : String(e) };\n  }\n}\n\nexport async function GET() {\n  const apiKey = process.env.NB_API_KEY;\n  if (!apiKey || apiKey === \"your_api_key_here\") {\n    return Response.json({ error: \"NB_API_KEY not configured (.env.local)\" }, { status: 500 });\n  }\n  const codes = listTerminals().map((t) => t.terminal);\n  if (codes.length === 0) return Response.json({ error: \"no terminals found\" }, { status: 400 });\n\n  const results = await Promise.all(codes.map((c) => solveTerminal(c, apiKey)));\n\n  const wb = XLSX.utils.book_new();\n  const bold = { font: { bold: true } };\n\n  // Per-terminal summary sheet.\n  const sumHeader = [\"TERMINAL\", \"STOPS\", \"ROUTES\", \"UNASSIGNED\", \"TOTAL_DIST_KM\", \"AVG_ROUTE_TIME\", \"TARGET\"];\n  const sumAoa: (string | number | null)[][] = [sumHeader.map((v) => ({ v, s: bold })) as unknown as (string | number)[]];\n  // Per-route detail sheet.\n  const detHeader = [\"TERMINAL\", \"ROUTE\", \"STOPS\", \"DURATION\", \"DISTANCE_KM\", \"WEIGHT_KG\", \"PARCELS\"];\n  const detAoa: (string | number | null)[][] = [detHeader.map((v) => ({ v, s: bold })) as unknown as (string | number)[]];\n\n  for (const r of results) {\n    if (\"error\" in r && r.error) {\n      sumAoa.push([r.code, null, null, null, null, null, `ERROR: ${r.error}`]);\n      continue;\n    }\n    const routes = r.routes!;\n    const totDist = routes.reduce((a, rt) => a + (rt.distance ?? 0), 0);\n    const avgDur = routes.length ? routes.reduce((a, rt) => a + (rt.duration ?? 0), 0) / routes.length : 0;\n    sumAoa.push([r.code, r.terminal!.stops.length, routes.length, r.unassigned!, km(totDist), hms(avgDur), hms(r.terminal!.targetRouteSeconds)]);\n    routes.forEach((rt, i) => {\n      const stops = (rt.steps ?? []).filter((s) => s.type === \"job\" || s.type === \"pickup\" || s.type === \"delivery\").length;\n      detAoa.push([\n        r.code, i + 1, stops, hms(rt.duration), km(rt.distance),\n        (rt.delivery?.[0] ?? 0) + (rt.pickup?.[0] ?? 0), (rt.delivery?.[1] ?? 0) + (rt.pickup?.[1] ?? 0),\n      ]);\n    });\n  }\n\n  const sumWs = XLSX.utils.aoa_to_sheet(sumAoa);\n  sumWs[\"!cols\"] = sumHeader.map((h) => ({ wch: Math.max(12, h.length + 1) }));\n  XLSX.utils.book_append_sheet(wb, sumWs, \"Terminal Summary\");\n  const detWs = XLSX.utils.aoa_to_sheet(detAoa);\n  detWs[\"!cols\"] = detHeader.map((h) => ({ wch: Math.max(11, h.length + 1) }));\n  XLSX.utils.book_append_sheet(wb, detWs, \"Routes\");\n\n  const buf = XLSX.write(wb, { type: \"buffer\", bookType: \"xlsx\" }) as Buffer;\n  return new Response(new Uint8Array(buf), {\n    status: 200,\n    headers: {\n      \"Content-Type\": \"application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet\",\n      \"Content-Disposition\": `attachment; filename=\"dhl_pl_tactical_planning.xlsx\"`,\n    },\n  });\n}\n"
}
```

### CLAUDE (2026-07-16T16:12:24.388Z)

PT is a large fleet-minimization problem and NB is still solving it (the fixed-cost objective makes it work harder to pack tightly). The full feature is built and verified except this final model-quality check. Let me summarize where things stand while the background poll (which will report PT's route count and durations) finishes.

## Built and verified
**Multi-tab UI** — confirmed live: both tabs render (`PLIK 1 - Daily Route Planning`, `PLIK 2 - Tactical Planning`); PLIK 1 still works (227 route-days); tactical API lists PT/LU/RZ.

**PLIK 2 — Tactical Planning** (new):
- `scripts/build-terminals.mjs` → `data/terminals/{PT,LU,RZ}.json` (1,830 / 5,707 / 5,675 stops; null & 0,0 coords excluded).
- `src/lib/terminal-data.ts`, `src/lib/plik2-input.ts` — capacitated fleet-sizing VRP: one vehicle pool per terminal, each capped at **7 h** `max_working_time`, capacity **[1400 kg, 500 pcs]**, high per-vehicle `costs.fixed` to minimize route count. Service = `TIME FOR STOP` + per-package time; delivery/pickup demand; `TIME FROM/TO` windows.
- `/api/tactical` (submit) + `/api/tactical/all` (Excel: Terminal Summary + per-Route sheets).
- `Plik2.tsx` — terminal selector, "Determine routes", stat tiles (routes required, stops served, avg time, distance) + per-route table, and "Run all → Excel".

## Model tuning note
My first PT run under-provisioned vehicles (28 offered, all used, **53 unassigned**), and routes averaged only ~4 h — the solver spread work into many short routes. I revised it: **larger pool (39 vehicles) + a high fixed cost per vehicle** to pack routes toward 7 h. That re-solve is what's still running.

I'll confirm PT's final route count / durations the moment the solve returns. One thing to flag up front: **LU and RZ have ~5,700 stops each** — those are very large VRPs and will take several minutes (possibly longer than PT) to solve; the "Run all → Excel" over all three is a long-running call. If PT's numbers look right, I'll note whether LU/RZ are practical to solve as-is or need the problem split (e.g., by sub-area) for reasonable solve times.

- Updated the **Dockerfile** to ship `public/` (the map) and both data dirs, with `DHL_DATA_DIR=/data/routes` and `DHL_TERMINAL_DIR=/data/terminals`.

## Verified live
All three tab labels render; the map serves at **HTTP 200, 5,458,389 bytes, text/html**; and the other tabs are unaffected (PLIK 1 = 227 route-days, PLIK 2 = LU/PT/RZ).

## One bug worth knowing about
Dropping the 5.4 MB HTML into the project **hung the build indefinitely** — Tailwind v4 auto-scans project files for class names and sat at 99% CPU parsing that file (I killed it at 4+ minutes). Fixed by excluding `public/` from Tailwind's content scan in `globals.css`:

```css
@source not "../../public";
```

Build went from hanging → **5 seconds**. Worth remembering if you add more large static assets — anything big in `public/` needs to stay outside Tailwind's scan.

## When to use

Shipping a containerized NB.ai demo (`/nb-demo-app-scaffold`) to GCP Cloud Run. Used by DIESEL_DIRECT, SCA, GLWAS.

## File layout

```
<VERTICAL>/
  Dockerfile                # multi-stage Next.js standalone build
  terraform/
    main.tf                 # APIs, Artifact Registry, Secret Manager, Cloud Run v2
    variables.tf            # project_id, region, service_name, image, nb_api_key, ...
    outputs.tf              # service_url, image_repository, build_and_push_command
    terraform.tfvars        # gitignored; contains nb_api_key + project_id
    terraform.tfvars.example
```

Copy these from `SCA/terraform/` for new verticals. The terraform is ~150 lines total and rarely needs deeper changes.

## Dockerfile (multi-stage, Next.js standalone)

```dockerfile
FROM node:20-alpine AS deps
WORKDIR /app
COPY demo/package.json demo/package-lock.json* ./
RUN npm ci

FROM node:20-alpine AS builder
WORKDIR /app
ARG NEXT_PUBLIC_NB_MAP_KEY=""
ENV NEXT_PUBLIC_NB_MAP_KEY=${NEXT_PUBLIC_NB_MAP_KEY}
ENV NEXT_TELEMETRY_DISABLED=1
COPY --from=deps /app/node_modules ./node_modules
COPY demo/ ./
RUN npm run build

FROM node:20-alpine AS runner
WORKDIR /app
ENV NODE_ENV=production
ENV NEXT_TELEMETRY_DISABLED=1
ENV HOSTNAME=0.0.0.0
ENV PORT=8080
RUN addgroup -S app && adduser -S app -G app
COPY --from=builder --chown=app:app /app/.next/standalone ./
COPY --from=builder --chown=app:app /app/.next/static ./.next/static
COPY --from=builder --chown=app:app /app/public ./public
COPY --chown=app:app data /data           # bake customer data into image
ENV DATA_DIR=/data
USER app
EXPOSE 8080
CMD ["node", "server.js"]
```

`next.config.ts` must set `output: 'standalone'` for the `.next/standalone` directory to exist.

## Deploy sequence

```bash
# From <VERTICAL>/ (parent of demo/ and terraform/):
export PROJECT=<gcp-project>
export REGION=us-central1
export REPO=<vertical-lower>          # e.g. "sca"
export SVC=<vertical-lower>-demo      # e.g. "sca-demo"
export TAG=$(date +%Y%m%d-%H%M%S)
IMG="$REGION-docker.pkg.dev/$PROJECT/$REPO/$SVC:$TAG"

gcloud auth configure-docker "$REGION-docker.pkg.dev"

# CRITICAL: --platform=linux/amd64 on M1/M2 Macs or Cloud Run will fail to start
docker build --platform=linux/amd64 \
  --build-arg NEXT_PUBLIC_NB_MAP_KEY="$NB_MAP_KEY" \
  -t "$IMG" .
docker push "$IMG"

cd terraform
terraform apply -auto-approve -var image="$IMG"
terraform output service_url
```

## CRITICAL gotchas

- **`-var image=...` is REQUIRED on every apply.** `variables.tf` defaults `image` to the GCP "hello" sample so the first apply succeeds before the image exists. If you forget the flag on subsequent applies, terraform silently resets the Cloud Run service back to the placeholder. **Always pass `-var image=...:<TAG>`.**
- **`--platform=linux/amd64` is non-negotiable on M1/M2 Macs.** Cloud Run won't start an arm64 image.
- **`NEXT_PUBLIC_NB_MAP_KEY` is build-time.** Pass it via `--build-arg` during `docker build`, not as a Cloud Run env var. Rotating it requires a rebuild + push.
- **`NB_API_KEY` is runtime.** Wired through Secret Manager (`<service>-nb-api-key` secret); terraform creates the secret with `var.nb_api_key` as the initial version. Update via `gcloud secrets versions add` then redeploy (Cloud Run pins to a specific secret version unless you set `version = "latest"`, which `SCA/terraform/main.tf` does — so a new version takes effect on next instance start).
- **`allow_unauthenticated = true`** is the demo default. Auth is handled at app level via cookie middleware (`/nb-demo-app-scaffold`). Switching this to false breaks the demo.
- **Cold start is 3–8s** with `min_instances = 0`. To eliminate it, set `min_instances = 1` in tfvars (costs ~$30/mo per always-on instance). A Cloud Scheduler pinger sounds appealing but adds operational complexity for marginal savings — prefer `min_instances = 1` if cold start matters.

## terraform/main.tf key blocks

```hcl
locals {
  required_apis = toset([
    "run.googleapis.com",
    "artifactregistry.googleapis.com",
    "secretmanager.googleapis.com",
    "iam.googleapis.com",
  ])
}

resource "google_project_service" "apis" {
  for_each           = local.required_apis
  service            = each.value
  disable_on_destroy = false           # don't disable APIs on terraform destroy
}

resource "google_cloud_run_v2_service" "app" {
  name     = var.service_name
  location = var.region
  ingress  = "INGRESS_TRAFFIC_ALL"
  deletion_protection = false
  template {
    service_account = google_service_account.run_sa.email
    scaling {
      min_instance_count = var.min_instances
      max_instance_count = var.max_instances
    }
    containers {
      image = var.image                # ← THE TRAP. always override with -var.
      env { name = "NB_API_KEY"
        value_source { secret_key_ref {
          secret  = google_secret_manager_secret.nb_api_key.secret_id
          version = "latest"
        }}
      }
    }
  }
  lifecycle { ignore_changes = [client, client_version] }
}
```

Copy `SCA/terraform/main.tf` whole for any new vertical — it's 150 lines and the right shape.

## Tag convention

`YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS` UTC. Don't use `:latest` — `:latest` makes rollbacks impossible because Cloud Run resolves the digest at deploy time, not at instance start.

## Rollback

```bash
# List recent images
gcloud artifacts docker images list "$REGION-docker.pkg.dev/$PROJECT/$REPO/$SVC" \
  --include-tags --sort-by=~CREATE_TIME --limit 10

# Redeploy a specific tag
terraform apply -auto-approve -var image="$REGION-docker.pkg.dev/$PROJECT/$REPO/$SVC:<OLD_TAG>"
```

## Reference implementations

- `SCA/terraform/` + `SCA/Dockerfile` — current canonical
- `DIESEL_DIRECT/terraform/` + `Dockerfile`
- `GLWAS/terraform/` + `Dockerfile`

Pairs with: `/nb-demo-app-scaffold` (the thing you're deploying).

### CLAUDE (2026-07-17T12:54:41.220Z)

Terraform for Cloud Run is ready and validated.

## Created — `DHL_PL/terraform/`
Following the canonical `SCA/terraform/` pattern from the deploy skill: `main.tf`, `variables.tf`, `outputs.tf`, `versions.tf`, `terraform.tfvars.example`, `.gitignore`.

It provisions: required APIs → Artifact Registry (`dhl-pl`) → Secret Manager → service account + IAM → Cloud Run v2 (`dhl-pl-demo`) → public invoker.

**DHL-specific choices (vs. the SCA template):**
- **No `NEXT_PUBLIC_NB_MAP_KEY`** — this demo has no MapLibre map; the Strategic Planning tab is a static iframe baked into the image.
- **Optional `NB_BFF_TOKEN` secret** — conditionally created (`count`/`dynamic env`) so the PLIK 1 `SHARED_URL` column works. Verified: **11 resources without it, 14 with**.
- **`timeout = 3600s`** (Cloud Run max) — your batch endpoints are long-running (PLIK 1 solves 227 route-days; PLIK 2 solves ~5,700-job terminals that took minutes each).
- **cpu 2 / memory 2Gi** — PLIK 2 builds very large optimization bodies plus Excel exports.
- Env `DHL_DATA_DIR=/data/routes`, `DHL_TERMINAL_DIR=/data/terminals` matching the Dockerfile.

## Two gaps I found and fixed
1. **`DHL_PL` had no `.dockerignore`** — the Dockerfile's `COPY demo/ ./` would have **baked `.env.local` (your API key + BFF token) into the image**. Added one; verified `.env.local`, `node_modules`, `.next`, and `terraform/` are excluded while `data/` and `public/` (the map) still ship.
2. **Terraform validate rejected `shared_urls_enabled`** — it inherits sensitivity from `nb_bff_token`. Fixed with `nonsensitive()`, since the boolean only reveals *whether* a token was supplied.

## Verified
`terraform fmt` clean · `terraform validate` → **Success** · `plan` runs cleanly against `[GCP_PROJECT]` · `terraform.tfvars`, `.terraform/`, and `.env.local` all git-ignored.

## To deploy
```bash
cd DHL_PL/terraform
cp terraform.tfvars.example terraform.tfvars   # set project_id + nb_api_key
terraform init && terraform apply              # placeholder image first

cd ..                                          # DHL_PL/ = build context
export TAG=$(date -u +%Y%m%d-%H%M%S)
IMG="us-central1-docker.pkg.dev/<PROJECT>/dhl-pl/dhl-pl-demo:$TAG"
gcloud auth configure-docker us-central1-docker.pkg.dev
docker build --platform=linux/amd64 -t "$IMG" . && docker push "$IMG"
cd terraform && terraform apply -var image="$IMG"
```

⚠️ Per the skill's main trap: **pass `-var image=…` on every apply** — omitting it silently resets the service to the placeholder hello image. And `--platform=linux/amd64` is required on your Mac or Cloud Run won't start the container.

I stopped short of actually building/pushing/applying since that's an outward-facing deploy to your GCP project — say the word and I'll run it.

### CLAUDE (2026-07-17T13:42:57.848Z)

Terraform **is** installed — `/opt/homebrew/bin/terraform`, v1.14.4. So it's not a missing binary.

The giveaway is the error itself: `command not found:  terraform` — there's a space *inside* the command name. Your shell is looking for a command literally called `<something>terraform`, which means an invisible character (usually a non-breaking space, U+00A0) got pasted in ahead of it. That happens when copying a command out of rendered markdown.

Just retype it by hand rather than pasting:

```
terraform init && terraform apply
```

If it still fails, that would mean `/opt/homebrew/bin` isn't on your interactive shell's PATH (my tool's environment and your zsh can differ). Check with `echo $PATH | tr ':' '\n' | grep homebrew`, and worst case invoke it directly:

```
/opt/homebrew/bin/terraform init && /opt/homebrew/bin/terraform apply
```

Also worth remembering: `init` is already done in this directory (I ran it to validate), and you'll need `terraform.tfvars` with `project_id` + `nb_api_key` before `apply` will get past the prompts.

## Contents
1. **Getting started** — deployed URL vs. local run, the API-key requirement, how the tab bar behaves.
2. **PLIK 1 — Daily Route Planning** — purpose (and why there's no planned-vs-optimized comparison), the data (47 routes × 5 dates = 227 route-days), step-by-step Route → Date → **Optimize route**, how to read the header/status pill/request id/stop table, the full **Run all → Excel** column reference, and the model table (07:00 Warsaw shift start, service = `TIME FOR STOP`, `TIME START`–`TIME STOP` windows, truck profile, 0,0-coord exclusions).
3. **PLIK 2 — Tactical Planning** — the fleet-sizing question, the three terminals (PT 1,830 / LU 5,707 / RZ 5,675), **Determine routes**, the summary tiles and per-route table, both Excel sheets, and the constraint table (7 h `max_working_time`, 1,400 kg, 500 pcs, per-package service). Includes the two honest caveats: **some stops are unassignable** (PT's 265 km cluster needs a ~9 h round trip) and **routes won't all be 7 h** because geography forces travel-dominated routes.
4. **Strategic Planning** — the depot-allocation map, how to use it, no API key needed.
5. **Refreshing data** (`build-routes` / `build-terminals`), **Configuration** (all four env vars), **Troubleshooting** table, and **Deployment** notes.

I verified every label, column, and constant against the source rather than writing from memory.

## One bug I found and fixed while documenting
I was about to write "you can leave a tab and come back while it solves" — then checked, and `page.tsx` was **unmounting the inactive tab**, which would silently discard an in-flight run. Since PLIK 2 solves take *minutes*, that's a real usability problem.

Fixed: tabs now mount on first visit and stay mounted (hidden when inactive), so runs survive tab switches. A bonus — mounting lazily means the **5.4 MB map is no longer loaded until Strategic Planning is opened**. Verified: 0 references to the map in the initial HTML, still served on demand (HTTP 200, 5,458,389 bytes), all three tabs render, build clean.

Login page added, matching the GLWAS pattern.

## Three files ported (cookie renamed `glwas_demo_auth` → `dhl_pl_demo_auth`, title updated)
- **`src/middleware.ts`** — gates everything except `/login` and `/api/login`. Pages redirect to `/login?next=…`; API calls get `401 {"error":"unauthorized"}`.
- **`src/app/login/page.tsx`** — the email/password form.
- **`src/app/api/login/route.ts`** — `POST` validates and sets a 7-day HttpOnly cookie; `DELETE` clears it.

Defaults are the same as GLWAS: **`[EMAIL]` / `[REDACTED_SECRET]`**, overridable via `DEMO_USER`, `DEMO_PASS`, `DEMO_AUTH_TOKEN`.

## Verified end-to-end
Unauthenticated `/` → `307` to `/login?next=%2F` · unauthenticated API → `401` · `/login` → `200` · bad creds → `401` · good creds → cookie set · then `/` → `200`, `/api/routes` → 227 route-days, map → `200`. Build clean.

Worth noting: the middleware also gates the **Strategic Planning map** (`/depot_allocation_map_6.html`), so it's no longer publicly fetchable — it only loads for a signed-in session via the iframe.

## Also updated
- **terraform** — added `demo_user` / `demo_pass` / `demo_auth_token` variables, injected as env vars (plan confirms **3 new `+ env` blocks**; contents redacted because two are `sensitive`). Corrected the `allow_unauthenticated` description, which claimed this demo had no app-level auth — it does now.
- **`.env.local.example`** and the **User Manual** (new "Signing in" section, the three env vars in Configuration, and three login troubleshooting rows).

## One thing to be aware of
The login lives in **application code**, so it ships in the image. Your service is currently running `dhl-pl-demo:20260717-134713`, which predates this — a plain `terraform apply` will add the env vars but **not** the login. To activate it you need a fresh build:

```bash
cd DHL_PL
export TAG=$(date -u +%Y%m%d-%H%M%S)
IMG="us-central1-docker.pkg.dev/[GCP_PROJECT]/dhl-pl/dhl-pl-demo:$TAG"
docker build --platform=linux/amd64 -t "$IMG" . && docker push "$IMG"
cd terraform && terraform apply -var image="$IMG"
```

(My plan runs used dummy vars purely for validation — I never applied them.)

### CLAUDE (2026-07-17T14:36:12.570Z)

PDF created at **`DHL_PL/USER_MANUAL.pdf`** — 8 pages, A4, 360 KB.

## How I built it
`pandoc` (markdown → HTML) + a custom print stylesheet + **headless Chrome** `--print-to-pdf`. I chose that over pandoc's LaTeX engine deliberately: the manual has wide tables with long prose cells (which LaTeX overflows) plus Polish characters and glyphs like `▶ ■ → ×` — the browser handles both correctly via system fonts.

The styling picks up DHL brand cues: yellow table headers, a red title rule, zebra rows, styled code blocks, and highlighted callouts. It's set to avoid breaking rows across pages and to repeat table headers.

## Two defects I caught and fixed
1. **Duplicated title** — pandoc's `--metadata title` injected its own `<h1>` on top of the markdown's `#` heading, so page 1 showed the title twice. Switched to `pagetitle` only (sets `<title>` without the extra heading).
2. **"Required" split mid-word** as `Requ/ired` — my `overflow-wrap: anywhere` let Chrome break ordinary words and collapse that column. Now only `code` tokens break anywhere; headers stay intact.

## Verified
8 pages · correct A4 (595×842pt) · text extracts cleanly including `Piotrków`/`Głogów`/`max_working_time`/`SHARED_URL` · title appears once · no table overflow — checked pages 1, 2, 7, 8 visually.

Note the PDF is a snapshot — if you edit `USER_MANUAL.md`, regenerate it. Happy to add a small `npm run manual-pdf` script if you'd like it reproducible, or add page numbers/footer (Chrome's CLI only offers its default footer, which includes an ugly `file://` path, so I left it clean).

Wed (\"4\"),\n      always honoring the POS's own `days_allowed` restriction.\n  R4  One service level (channel) per salesperson - never mixed.\n\nThe number of salespeople per service level is derived from a target average\ncustomers per rep: reps = ceil(customers_in_level / target).\n\nPOS model (parsed from each job's description):\n  {client}-{wk}-{visit}|{service_min}|WK-{n}|WK-VISIT-{k}|{days_allowed}|{channel}\n  - Unknown digits ignored.\"\"\"\n    days = set()\n    for ch in str(code):\n        if ch.isdigit() and int(ch) in DOW_TO_IDX:\n            days.add(DOW_TO_IDX[int(ch)])\n    return days or set(range(5))  # empty/garbage -> unrestricted\n\n\ndef parse_pos(data):\n    loc = data[\"locations\"][\"location\"]\n    pos = {}\n    for j in data[\"jobs\"]:\n        d = str(j[\"description\"]).split(\"|\")\n        if len(d) < 6:\n            continue\n        client = d[0].split(\"-\")[0]\n        service_min = int(d[1]) if d[1].isdigit() else 0\n        week = int(d[2].split(\"-\")[-1]) if d[2].startswith(\"WK-\") else 1\n        visit = int(d[3].split(\"-\")[-1]) if d[3].startswith(\"WK-VISIT-\") else 1\n        allowed = parse_days_allowed(d[4])\n        channel = d[5]\n        p = pos.get(client)\n        if p is None:\n            p = pos[client] = POS(client)\n            p.channel = channel\n            lat, lng = (float(x) for x in loc[j[\"location_index\"]].split(\",\"))\n            p.lat, p.lng, p.service_min = lat, lng, service_min\n        p.allowed |= allowed\n        p.freq = max(p.freq, visit)\n        p.jobs_by_week[week].append(j)\n    # freq is the number of visits/week the data actually carries.\n    return pos\n\n\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n# R2/R4: balanced, channel-pure territories\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\ndef balanced_kmeans(coords, k, iters=25, seed=0):\n    \"\"\"Capacity-balanced k-means. ### CLAUDE (2026-07-17T17:43:15.524Z)

Now I understand the real issue — it's **genuine data infeasibility**, not a bug. Those 9 reps are geographic clusters whose customers *all* forbid the missing day (e.g., a whole area of Mon/Thu-only POS with zero Wednesday-permitting customers). R1 (cover Mon–Fri) conflicts with R3 (honor `days_allowed`) for such territories.

The right fix honoring R1's intent: **swap POS across neighboring same-channel reps** so a rep missing a day gains a nearby customer that permits it (1-for-1, keeping counts balanced). Let me add that repair step:

Returns #moves.\"\"\"\n    rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)\n    by_channel = defaultdict(list)\n    for rid, r in reps.items():\n        by_channel[r[\"channel\"]].append(rid)\n    moves = 0\n    for _ in range(max_passes):\n        changed = False\n        # process smallest reps first so donors stay the larger ones\n        for rid in sorted(reps, key=lambda x: len(reps[x][\"pos\"])):\n            r = reps[rid]\n            load = [0] * 5\n            for p in r[\"pos\"]:\n                for d in p.days:\n                    load[d] += 1\n            missing = [d for d in range(5) if load[d] == 0]\n            if not missing:\n                continue\n            cy, cx = _centroid(r[\"pos\"])\n            for d in missing:\n                my_size = len(r[\"pos\"])\n                best, best_from, bestdist = None, None, float(\"inf\")\n                for oid in by_channel[r[\"channel\"]]:\n                    if oid == rid or len(reps[oid][\"pos\"]) <= my_size:\n                        continue  # only take from a rep at least as large\n                    for p in reps[oid][\"pos\"]:\n                        if d in p.allowed:\n                            dist = (p.lat - cy) ** 2 + (p.lng - cx) ** 2\n                            if dist < bestdist:\n                                best, best_from, bestdist = p, oid, dist\n                if best is None:\n                    continue  # no eligible donor / globally infeasible\n                reps[best_from][\"pos\"].remove(best); pos_by_rep[best_from].remove(best)\n                best.rep = rid; r[\"pos\"].append(best); pos_by_rep[rid].append(best)\n                moves += 1\n                changed = True\n                reps[rid][\"load\"] = assign_days_for_rep(r[\"pos\"], rng)\n                reps[best_from][\"load\"] = assign_days_for_rep(reps[best_from][\"pos\"], rng)\n        if not changed:\n            break\n    return moves"
}

## New script: `COCA_COLA-FEMSA/data/rolling_horizon_territories.py`

The "assignment then optimize" variant. **Phase 1** designs the salesperson territories enforcing all four rules; **Phase 2** emits a fixed-territory input the existing `rolling_horizon.py` can run.

### How it satisfies each rule
- **R4 (one service level per rep):** POS are partitioned by **channel** first; every territory is channel-pure by construction.
- **R2 (balanced customers):** within each channel, a capacity-balanced k-means (pure numpy) splits POS into `ceil(count / target)` reps of near-equal size.
- **R3 (service groups):** 2×/week POS → Mon+Thu (`25`) or Tue+Fri (`36`), chosen to balance daily load; 1×/week POS → a single weekday incl. Wed (`4`); every choice honors the POS's own `days_allowed`.
- **R1 (Mon–Fri coverage):** each rep first seeds coverage, then a cross-territory repair pulls in the nearest permitting customer from a neighbor where a territory is inherently day-restricted.

### Verified (independently, from the output CSVs)
```
reps: 102 | customers/rep min/mean/max: 45/63.5/68
r1_missing_weekday: 0  r3_bad_biweekly: 0  r3_day_not_allowed: 0  r4_mixed_channel: 0
ALL RULES SATISFIED
```
Within each channel the balance is tight (TRADICIONAL 65, NOTURNO 63, AUTOSSERVICO 47–48); the spread is only channel-size differences, well clear of the "20 vs 40" case. Runs in ~1 s, and works at other targets (`--target-per-rep 50` → 131 reps, all rules satisfied).

### Output (`territories_out/`)
- `territories.csv` — rep, channel, customers, per-weekday visit counts, Mon–Fri coverage flag.
- `pos_assignments.csv` — every POS → rep + assigned days.
- `input_territories.json` (with `--fixed-input`) — 19,370 jobs each pinned to its rep's zone and its single assigned weekday; 2,040 rep-day vehicles restricted to their own zone. Ready for `rolling_horizon.py --no-zones --input …`.

## Three real modeling issues I hit and fixed
1. **R1 vs R3 conflict:** 9 territories were geographic clusters of Mon/Thu-only (`25`) customers with *zero* Wednesday-permitting POS — R1 is literally impossible from their own customers. Solved by cross-territory swaps that pull a nearby permitting customer in (kept balanced).
2. **Thrashing (195 swaps, net zero):** all-restricted reps stole coverage POS back and forth. Fixed with a donor-safety guard — only pull a POS whose removal won't uncover a day for its donor → **19 clean swaps**.
3. **2× can't cover Wed:** the repair was pulling biweekly POS that lock to Mon+Thu/Tue+Fri and never land on Wednesday; restricted the pull to 1× POS.

## Two notes
- I used **`--target-per-rep 65`** as a placeholder (≈ 6,481/100). You said you'd give the exact target — set it and re-run; everything scales.
- I built and validated the assignment + the fixed-territory input, but did **not** run the Phase-2 optimization itself (`rolling_horizon.py --no-zones`), since that drives the existing simulator/NB-clustering pipeline. import json, glob
from collections import defaultdict
# map job id -> zone, vehicle id -> allowed zone, from the pinned input
inp=json.load(open("territories_out/input_territories.json"))
job_zone={j["id"]: j["zones"][0] for j in inp["jobs"]}
veh_zone={v["id"]: v["allowed_zones"][0] for v in inp["vehicles"]}
veh_desc={v["id"]: v["description"] for v in inp["vehicles"]}

tot_dist=tot_dur=tot_service=0; tot_stops=0; breaches=0; routes=0
per_day=[]
for f in sorted(glob.glob("territories_out/sim_runs/day_0[1-5]_output.json")):
    o=json.load(open(f))
    d_dist=d_stops=0; d_routes=0
    for rt in o.get("routes",[]):
        d_routes+=1; routes+=1
        vz=veh_zone.get(rt["vehicle"])
        for s in rt.get("steps",[]):
            if s.get("type")=="job":
                d_stops+=1; tot_stops+=1
                # territory adherence: served job's zone must match vehicle's zone
                if job_zone.get(s["id"]) != vz: breaches+=1
        d_dist+=rt.get("distance",0)
    summ=o.get("summary",{})
    tot_dist+=summ.get("distance",0); tot_dur+=summ.get("duration",0); tot_service+=summ.get("service",0)
    per_day.append((f.split("/")[-1], d_routes, d_stops, round(summ.get("distance",0)/1000)))
print("day                routes  stops  dist_km")
for n,r,s,km in per_day: print(f"  {n:<18} {r:>4}  {s:>5}  {km:>6}")
print(f"\nWEEK 1 totals: routes={routes}, job-stops={tot_stops}, distance={tot_dist/1000:.0f} km, drive={tot_dur/3600:.0f} h, service={tot_service/3600:.0f} h")
print(f"territory breaches (job served outside its rep's zone): {breaches}  <- must be 0")
PY

### CLAUDE (2026-07-17T18:05:06.117Z)

Week 1 ran end-to-end and the territories held perfectly. Here's the result.

## Week 1 optimization — `territories_out/`

Ran `rolling_horizon.py --no-zones` on the fixed-territory input for the first 5 days (2026-07-20 → 07-24, Mon–Fri):

| Day | Routes | Stops served | Distance |
|---|---|---|---|
| Mon 07-20 | 102 | 1,486 | 2,040 km |
| Tue 07-21 | 102 | 1,389 | 1,694 km |
| Wed 07-22 | 102 | 1,265 | 1,741 km |
| Thu 07-23 | 102 | 1,488 | 1,903 km |
| Fri 07-24 | 102 | 1,388 | 1,699 km |
| **Total** | **510** | **7,016** | **9,075 km** (296 h drive, 1,145 h service) |

**Territory integrity verified: 0 breaches** — every one of the 7,016 served jobs was handled by a vehicle whose zone matched the job's rep, so the fixed territories held exactly. Each day used all **102 routes** (one per salesperson), confirming R1 (every rep works Mon–Fri) plays out operationally.

**97 jobs expired** (~1.4% of the 7,113 week-1 jobs): 43 Mon, 41 Tue, then 8/4/1 — these couldn't be fit within their single assigned day inside their territory (the day-pinned windows mean an unfit visit can't roll to another day). The tail dropping to 1 by Friday is the expected pattern.

## Fixes needed to make the handoff work
Two schema issues surfaced when feeding the assignment into the existing simulator:
1. **Relative paths broke** under the simulator's `cwd=REPO_ROOT` — needed absolute `--workdir`/`--simulator`.
2. **The simulator wants integer vehicle ids** (`uint64`), but I'd used descriptive strings. Fixed `build_fixed_input` to number vehicles 1…N (readable label moved to `description`) and to carry `capacity`/`max_working_time`/`max_completion_time` from a template so demand constraints still apply. Regenerated the input.

The run command (from the data dir, with absolute paths) is:
```bash
.venv/bin/python rolling_horizon.py --no-zones \
  --input "$PWD/territories_out/input_territories.json" \
  --workdir "$PWD/territories_out/sim_runs" \
  --simulator "$PWD/sim_runs/simulator" \
  --days 5 --limit-s 60
```

Want me to run the full 4 weeks (`--days 20`), or look into reducing the 97 expirations (e.g., raising `--limit-s`, or allowing a same-week fallback day for hard-to-fit visits)?
